properties.title: Apartment 1, Redcliff Court, Cliff Road, Budleigh Salterton (ground-floor 2 double bed, share of freehold, own garage)

flags.text: GROUND FLOOR — ALL ON ONE LEVEL
DIRECT ACCESS ONTO THE SOUTH WEST COAST PATH
PRIVATE SUN TERRACE WITH SEA VIEWS

properties.body: A spacious ground-floor apartment in Redcliff Court, reached by the drive immediately before The Rosemullion Apartments on Cliff Road. Accommodation is a wide hallway with cloaks and airing cupboards, a 15ft 11in x 13ft 9in lounge with double-glazed doors onto a private sun terrace, kitchen, two double bedrooms, a bathroom/WC and a further separate WC. Gas central heating. The communal grounds are mature and look along the Budleigh seafront towards Otter Head, with direct access onto the South West Coast Path. A single garage in a separate block to the front is included, and there is visitors’ parking on site. Apartment 1 holds an equal share of the freehold; service charge and buildings insurance together run to about £240 per calendar month. Council tax band E. Chain-free. Note: Links flag these as draft particulars awaiting the vendor’s verification, so treat the detail as provisional.
properties.why: A second ground-floor flat in the same Redcliff Court block already on this list — see the £230,000 Bradleys-listed one — so worth comparing the two directly rather than treating either as the only option. This one has the better parking of the pair: a proper single garage rather than an allocated bay, which matters for bikes and kit. Share of freehold, no chain, all on one level, and coast path access straight off the communal grounds. It is dated inside and the outgoings are real money at roughly £2,880 a year, and — taking Bro 3’s point on the neighbouring flat — the sea view here is partial and along the coast rather than the panorama the phrase suggests.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A private sun terrace and direct access onto the South West Coast Path straight from the communal grounds, plus its own garage.

properties.aiTake: Ground-floor, share of freehold, its own garage and the coast path off the back lawn — practical and well located, but dated and carrying £240 a month in outgoings.

parking.note: A single garage in a separate garage block to the front of the development is included in the sale, plus visitors’ parking on site — confirmed in the listing. The garage is the genuinely useful part here: secure, lockable storage for bikes and kit rather than just a marked bay.

properties.title: Gibson Close, Exmouth (3-bed freehold terrace with garage, solar panels and a secluded sunny garden)

flags.text: HAS PARKING (garage in a nearby block)
SECLUDED SUNNY REAR GARDEN + OUTSIDE STORE

properties.body: A three-bedroom freehold terrace on Gibson Close, a quiet residential cul-de-sac in Exmouth. Entrance porch into a 15ft 8in x 13ft 2in lounge with the staircase rising from it, then a 15ft 8in kitchen/dining room fitted with a gas hob and built-in oven, running the full depth of the house with double doors opening onto the rear garden. Upstairs are three bedrooms — the main with a fitted wardrobe range and dressing table — and a bathroom/WC with shower over the bath and a heated towel rail. Double glazing, gas central heating and solar panels already installed. Front garden with a path and an outside store; the rear garden is the best bit, sunny and well screened, laid to lawn with a patio, stocked flower and shrub beds, a shed and an outside tap. A garage sits in a block close by.
properties.why: Three bedrooms, freehold, a garage and solar panels for under £270,000 is solid value in Exmouth, and the secluded sunny rear garden lifts it above the usual terrace. It is an ordinary modern house rather than anything characterful, which is where Bro 3 has consistently marked things down, and the garage being in a block rather than on the plot means day-to-day parking outside the door is still on-street in the close — worth checking how crowded that gets.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Solar panels already fitted — the running-cost saving is in place rather than something to budget for.

properties.aiTake: Three freehold bedrooms, a garage, solar and a genuinely nice private garden — sensible value, but a plain modern house with no character to speak of.

parking.note: A garage is included, located in a block close by rather than on the plot itself — Pennys do not give a distance, so ask how far it actually is. That means the garage is storage-and-security parking rather than parking at the door; day-to-day kerbside parking would be in Gibson Close itself, which is a quiet residential cul-de-sac off Hulham Road with no residents’ permit scheme, so it should be workable but is not guaranteed outside the house.

properties.title: Brackendale, Exmouth (2-bed freehold corner link house, two allocated parking spaces, move-in ready)

flags.text: HAS PARKING (2 allocated spaces at the front)

properties.body: An immaculate modern two-bedroom corner link house on Brackendale, in the Brixington area of north Exmouth. Ground floor is an entrance hall with a run of storage cupboards, a bay-fronted living room and a contemporary fitted kitchen with integrated electric oven, induction hob, washer/dryer and slimline dishwasher; upstairs are two well-proportioned bedrooms and a bathroom with a Mira electric shower over the bath. Double glazed and gas centrally heated, with a combi boiler fitted in January 2026. Outside there is a small enclosed garden laid to stone chippings with timber fencing, and two allocated parking spaces immediately in front of the property. Freehold, with a service charge noted on the particulars for the estate’s communal areas.
properties.why: Two allocated parking spaces on a freehold house at £230,000 is a genuinely good practical package, and it needs nothing doing — the boiler is eight months old and the kitchen is current. Against that, it is exactly the kind of blank modern box Bro 3 has repeatedly rated low, the garden is chippings rather than anything to sit in, and Brackendale is on the northern edge of town, so the seafront is a drive rather than a walk. A sensible fallback, not a find.
properties.aiTake: Freehold, two parking spaces and nothing to do to it — but a characterless modern box with a chippings yard, on the wrong edge of town for the sea.

parking.note: Two allocated parking spaces sit immediately in front of the property — confirmed in the listing and visible on the particulars. Two spaces on a two-bedroom house at this price is unusually generous and removes the parking question entirely.

properties.title: 52 Norman Crescent, Budleigh Salterton (ground-floor 2-bed, en-suite + bathroom, allocated parking)

flags.text: GROUND FLOOR — ALL ON ONE LEVEL

properties.body: A ground-floor two-bedroom apartment at 52 Norman Crescent, Budleigh Salterton (EX9 6RB), guide £192,000 with Red Homes and no chain. Communal doors front and rear with an entry phone lead to a private hallway. The lounge is 4.77m x 3.66m and bright with double-glazed windows, with a fitted kitchen of 3.55m x 1.63m alongside — inset sink, electric hob with extractor, fitted oven and space for freestanding appliances. The principal bedroom is a 3.55m x 2.72m double with its own en-suite shower room, and the second bedroom, 2.56m x 2.72m, has two built-in cupboards and would suit a guest room or office. There is a separate family bathroom with a panelled bath. Heating is by night storage and electric wall heaters rather than gas. Outside, the flat comes with one allocated parking space and residents share a well-managed gated lawned garden. Tenure is leasehold on a 155-year lease from 2003, so roughly 132 years remain — ground rent £167.71 per half year, service and management £453.07 per half year, and buildings insurance £261.96 a year, giving total outgoings of about £1,500 a year. Council tax band B, EPC C.
properties.why: This is the cheapest thing on the list that is genuinely ground-floor, has its own allocated parking, and gives two bedrooms and two bathrooms — at £192,000 it sits close to the real £170k target rather than the £300k ceiling. Budleigh puts it near the Otterton brother and an easy run to Exmouth. The trade-offs are that it is leasehold, and while 132 years is a comfortable term, roughly £1,500 a year of combined service charge, ground rent and insurance is a standing cost a freehold house would not carry; there is also no private garden, only the shared gated lawn, and no character in a 2003 block.

parking.note: One allocated parking space comes with the flat, alongside a gated communal lawned garden for residents.

properties.aiTake: Cheap, genuinely ground-floor, two beds and two bathrooms with its own parking space in Budleigh — the closest thing here to the real £170k target, docked for leasehold, ~£1,500/yr outgoings and no private garden or character.

properties.title: Chichester Close, Exmouth (1-bed semi-detached bungalow, driveway + garage, solar panels, park views)

flags.text: QUIET CUL-DE-SAC — VIEWS OVER PHEAR PARK

properties.body: A one-double-bedroom semi-detached bungalow tucked into a quiet cul-de-sac off Ashleigh Road on the edge of Exmouth, guide £225,000 freehold with Links, no onward chain. The layout is a single open-plan living room/kitchen of 17ft4 x 15ft2 with a breakfast bar, built-in electric hob and oven, and a window to the rear looking over the garden with Phear Park beyond. Off it is a 12ft5 x 9ft8 uPVC conservatory with French doors to the garden and views over Exmouth, a 13ft11 x 11ft6 double bedroom to the front, and a dual-aspect bathroom of 10ft7 x 5ft5 fitted with a four-piece suite including both a bath and a separate triple shower tray with a rainfall thermostatic shower. Gas central heating via a combi boiler, uPVC double glazing throughout, and solar panels are already fitted with the control unit indoors. The loft is insulated and part-boarded with its own double-glazed window, and the agent notes it could be converted for further accommodation subject to the usual consents. Outside is a driveway to the front leading to a detached garage, and a good-sized enclosed rear garden arranged over terraces. Council tax band B, about 452 sq ft.
properties.why: For the long-term brief this is one of the better shapes on the list — a genuine bungalow, so everything that matters is on one level, with a driveway, a detached garage for a workshop, a garden with a view over Phear Park, and solar panels already paid for by somebody else. The loft with a window and conversion potential is real upside on a small footprint. The obvious limit is that it is a one-bedroom house at 452 sq ft, so it works as a home for one but has no room for guests without converting that loft, and there are steps up from the driveway to the front door.

parking.note: Driveway to the front leading to a detached garage, which the agent describes as ideal for storage and would suit a workshop.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Solar panels already installed, plus an insulated, part-boarded loft with its own window flagged for conversion (STP).

properties.aiTake: A true one-level bungalow with driveway, detached garage, terraced garden, park views and solar panels already fitted — strong on the things that matter long-term, held back by being a single bedroom at 452 sq ft with no real character.

properties.title: Holly Walk, Exmouth (2-bed terrace, two parking spaces, sunny secluded rear garden, no chain)
properties.body: A two-bedroom terraced house on Holly Walk in the Brixington area of Exmouth, freehold at £235,000 with Pennys. Steps rise to the front door and an entrance hall opens into a 16ft10 x 11ft11 lounge/dining room with an alcove the agent suggests for a dining table or study, and a generous understairs cupboard. Behind it is a modern fitted kitchen of 11ft10 x 7ft3 with a wall-mounted Ideal gas boiler, plumbing for a washing machine and a door straight out to the garden. Upstairs are two bedrooms — 12ft10 x 8ft8 and 11ft4 x 6ft10 — and a bathroom/WC with a bath, shower and detachable hose. uPVC double glazing and gas central heating throughout, council tax band B. Outside, a decorative stone-chipped garden wraps the front and side, and the rear garden is enclosed with timber fencing, secluded and sunny-aspect, part lawn and part patio. Parking is the standout for the price: an allocated space at the front, plus a hardstanding parking area at the rear reached through a timber side gate, which the agent notes has the potential to become a garage or store subject to consents.
properties.why: Two parking spaces on a £235,000 freehold house is unusual, and the rear hardstanding with room for a garage is exactly the kind of workshop potential worth having. The garden is genuinely private and sunny rather than a token yard. The honest catch is that it is a straightforward modern terrace with no character to speak of, and Brixington sits a good mile and a half back from both the seafront and the station, so it trades charm and location for practicality and space.

parking.note: An allocated parking space at the front of the property, plus a separate hardstanding parking area at the rear accessed via a timber side gate — the agent notes this has potential to be converted into a garage or store subject to the usual consents.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Rear hardstanding with room to build a garage or workshop subject to planning — rare on a terrace at this price.

properties.aiTake: Freehold, two parking spaces, a secluded sunny garden and space to build a garage make this a lot of practical house for £235,000, but it has no character at all and sits well back from both the sea and the station.

properties.title: High Street, Newton Poppleford (Grade II listed 2-bed cottage, inglenook, garage + parking for several)

flags.text: ROOM FOR A CARAVAN OR BOAT

properties.body: A Grade II listed two-bedroom cottage on the High Street in Newton Poppleford, renovated and modernised by the current owners in recent years while keeping the character features intact. The ground floor has an entrance hall, a kitchen/diner with an inglenook-style fireplace and exposed timbers, and a sitting room; upstairs are two bedrooms and a modern bathroom/shower room. Gas radiator central heating throughout, and the vendor has confirmed buildings insurance is in place — worth noting, since insurance can be a sticking point on listed and thatched stock. Outside there is a detached single garage plus parking for several vehicles, a caravan or a boat, and a large private garden mainly laid to lawn with flower beds and a big patio. Newton Poppleford sits on the edge of the East Devon AONB with a primary school, post office, shop and pub, about four miles inland from Sidmouth and with easy access to the A3052.
properties.why: This is close to the shape of thing Jesse keeps saying he wants — a listed period cottage with real character features, already renovated so it isn't a money pit, and unusually generous parking for a village High Street property. The detached garage plus room for a caravan or boat is a lot of vehicle space for £250,000, and the large private garden is a genuine one rather than a yard. The catch is location: it's inland, about nine miles from Exmouth, with no train station in the village.

parking.note: Off-road parking for several vehicles plus a detached single garage, with the listing specifically calling out room for a caravan or boat. Unusually good for a High Street cottage and a clear pass on the hard requirement.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Parking for a caravan or boat alongside a detached garage — rare on a listed village High Street cottage

properties.aiTake: Renovated Grade II cottage with inglenook, a large private garden and far more parking than a village High Street usually offers, all freehold at £250,000 — held back mainly by being inland, with no train station and a fair drive to both the coast and the Woodbury brother.

properties.title: High Street, Newton Poppleford (2-bed barn conversion, single storey, allocated parking)

flags.text: SINGLE STOREY — ALL ON ONE LEVEL

properties.body: A two-bedroom barn conversion set in a small character courtyard development off the High Street in Newton Poppleford, presented as suitable either as a permanent home or a holiday let. All the accommodation is on a single storey, with character features including exposed beams, a kitchen with a built-in double oven and solid timber worktops, and two bedrooms both with fitted wardrobes. There is a large loft space above with potential to convert subject to planning, which is the obvious way to add value and space here. Double glazing throughout, electric heating, an allocated parking space and use of a communal garden. Freehold.
properties.why: A barn conversion is exactly the unconventional stock worth flagging rather than another generic modern semi, and being genuinely single storey makes it one of the stronger long-term-liveability options on the page. The convertible loft gives it somewhere to grow. The honest weaknesses are that the garden is communal rather than your own, and electric heating is the expensive way to heat a converted barn.

parking.note: An allocated parking space within the courtyard development, listed as a key feature.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A barn conversion in a small character courtyard, with a large loft that could be converted subject to planning

properties.aiTake: Genuinely unconventional — a single-storey barn conversion with exposed beams, allocated parking and a convertible loft — but the communal-only garden, electric heating and inland location keep it out of the top tier.

properties.title: The Marles, Exmouth (3-bed detached bungalow, corner plot, garage + driveway, estuary glimpses)

flags.text: DETACHED BUNGALOW — ALL ON ONE LEVEL
WRAPAROUND GARDEN ON A CORNER PLOT

properties.body: A three-bedroom detached bungalow on a generous corner plot in The Marles, one of Exmouth's more settled residential areas, with glimpses of the Exe Estuary. A porch leads into a wide hallway; to the left is a dual-aspect living room with large windows, and the modern kitchen opens directly onto the rear garden. Three good-sized bedrooms and a family bathroom sit off the hallway, with plenty of built-in storage. To the rear is a garage with a separate utility room alongside it. The garden wraps around the plot — low-maintenance patio at the back, lawns to the front and side. A gently sloped driveway provides off-road parking, with steps up to the front door. Freehold, well decorated and maintained throughout.
properties.why: Three bedrooms, detached, freehold, garage and driveway, on a corner plot in Exmouth itself for £250,000 is a lot of practical house for the money, and being a bungalow it clears the long-term stairs question outright. It is the least characterful thing in this batch — an ordinary well-kept bungalow rather than anything unusual — but on Jesse's actual checklist it ticks more boxes than most of the prettier options.

parking.note: A gently sloped driveway giving off-road parking, leading to a garage at the rear with a separate utility room beside it.

properties.aiTake: The most practical buy in this batch — 3-bed detached freehold bungalow in Exmouth with garage, driveway and a wraparound garden at £250,000 — but it has no real character, which is the one thing Jesse consistently says he's shopping for.

properties.title: Louisa Terrace, Exmouth (Grade II Georgian 2-bed lower ground floor, 999-yr lease + share of freehold, sea views)
properties.body: A Grade II listed Georgian two-bedroom lower ground floor apartment on Louisa Terrace, a short walk above Exmouth seafront. Around 860 sq ft — generous for the money — comprising a good-sized sitting room, a kitchen/dining room opening onto a small internal courtyard, two double bedrooms, a bathroom and a separate WC, plus two external store rooms. Gas central heating. The flat has a lawned front garden of its own with sea views, and Louisa Terrace is set back and slightly raised from the promenade rather than on it, which keeps it quieter than a seafront address usually is. Sold with no onward chain and with a brand-new 999-year lease and a share of the freehold, so in practical terms it behaves close to freehold. It does require a degree of updating.
properties.why: Georgian, listed, 860 sq ft, sea views and a private front garden, a couple of minutes from the beach, for £250,000 — and the new 999-year lease with share of freehold removes most of what Bro 3 dislikes about leasehold. It needs modernising, which is really the reason it's this price. The obvious gap is parking: there's none with the flat, and access is down external steps, which matters for the long-term stairs question.

parking.note: No parking comes with the flat. Louisa Terrace sits in central Exmouth, which has had a residents' parking permit scheme since 2023 — Devon County Council runs it through MiPermit, with first residents' permits around £35 a year for band A vehicles, so a permit is realistically obtainable and cheap if the address qualifies for its zone. Worth confirming with Devon CC which zone this end of Louisa Terrace falls in before committing, since the seafront streets carry heavy pay-and-display and summer visitor pressure and permit zones here were drawn street by street. Failing a permit, the Queen's Drive and seafront car parks are a short walk but are priced for tourists rather than residents.

research.question: What are the realistic parking options for a flat on Louisa Terrace with no allocated space?
research.findings: Devon County Council approved a residents' and business parking permit scheme for Exmouth after a consultation showing strong support, and three residents' parking zones went live in 2023, with a further consultation in late 2024 on adding zones in the Withycombe Road and Carter Avenue areas. Permits are administered digitally through MiPermit, with a first residents' permit costing roughly £35 a year for a band A vehicle and higher rates for additional permits and higher-emission vehicles. Louisa Terrace appears in Devon's MiPermit street listings, which indicates on-street controls apply there. The zones were drawn street by street rather than blanket-covering the town centre, so the specific zone and eligibility for this address should be checked directly against Devon CC's Exmouth traffic regulation orders before relying on it.

properties.aiTake: Listed Georgian character, 860 sq ft, sea views and a private front garden two minutes from Exmouth beach at £250,000, with a 999-year lease and share of freehold that neutralises most leasehold objections — docked for having no parking, needing modernisation, and being reached down external steps.

properties.title: Station Road, Newton Poppleford (2 double-bed character cottage, inglenook + wood burner, driveway, chain free)
properties.body: A two double-bedroom character cottage in the heart of Newton Poppleford, combining period features with modern services. The ground floor has a lounge/dining room extending over 20ft with an inglenook fireplace and wood-burning stove, exposed ceiling timbers and an understairs cupboard; to the rear is a modern fitted kitchen with built-in oven and hob and space for further appliances. Upstairs are two generous double bedrooms and a contemporary family bathroom. The enclosed rear garden is low maintenance, mixing paved patio and slate shingle, with pedestrian rear access that also leads to a private drive. Gas central heating and double glazing throughout, EPC C, freehold, no onward chain. Note this is a separate property from the Grade II* thatched cottage and barn already tracked on the same road — different house, different agent, £45,000 cheaper.
properties.why: At £215,000 this is one of the better character-per-pound propositions on the page, which is precisely the axis Bro 3 judges on: inglenook, wood burner and exposed timbers, but with an EPC C, modern kitchen and bathroom, gas central heating and no chain, so it isn't a renovation project with a hidden £70k attached. Freehold with a private drive. Same inland caveat as the rest of Newton Poppleford — no station, and a fair drive to Exmouth.

parking.note: Driveway parking listed as a key feature, reached via the pedestrian rear access — a private drive behind the cottage rather than on-street.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A 20ft lounge/dining room with inglenook fireplace and wood-burning stove — unusually large for a cottage at this price

properties.aiTake: Real cottage character — inglenook, wood burner, exposed timbers, 20ft living room — already modernised to EPC C with a private drive, freehold and chain free at £215,000; the only serious mark against it is being inland with no train station.

SHARE OF FREEHOLD, VERY LONG LEASE
A STONE'S THROW FROM EXMOUTH BEACH

properties.body: A one double-bedroom ground floor flat tucked away in a quiet mews courtyard behind Morton Crescent, a stone's throw from Exmouth beach. Inside there is a spacious bay-fronted lounge/dining room looking onto the garden, a fitted kitchen, a white-suite bathroom with shower over bath, and a double bedroom. uPVC double glazing and gas central heating. Outside it has its own private enclosed low-maintenance garden with room for furniture, level throughout, with the front door reached via a quiet courtyard at the back of 17 Morton Crescent. Held on a very long lease with a share of the freehold and a share in the management company; sold with no onward chain.
properties.why: £150,000 puts this comfortably inside Jesse's real target rather than the £300k ceiling, and it's ground floor, level, with its own private garden and a share of the freehold — the cheap-and-explicitly-ground-floor combination that makes a flat worth looking at. Being that close to the beach at this price is unusual. The two honest limits are that it's only one bedroom, and that the parking space isn't actually part of the sale.

parking.note: There is a small parking space outside the flat, but it is not included in the sale — the current owner rents it from the building's management company for a nominal annual sum, and happens to be a director of that company. The listing says a new owner could potentially rent it again but is explicit that this would need confirming with management at the time, so treat it as a maybe rather than a yes. Failing that, Morton Crescent sits in central Exmouth, where Devon County Council has run a residents' parking permit scheme since 2023 via MiPermit at roughly £35 a year for a first band A permit — worth checking directly with Devon CC whether this address qualifies for a zone, because seafront streets here carry heavy summer visitor pressure and the surrounding pay-and-display car parks are priced for tourists.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Its own private enclosed garden and a share of the freehold on a one-bed flat a stone's throw from Exmouth beach

properties.aiTake: Cheap, level, ground floor, with its own private garden and share of freehold right by Exmouth beach — the price is the main attraction, but one bedroom and a parking space that isn't actually included cap how far it goes.

properties.title: Elizabeth Road, Exmouth (2-bed semi-detached bungalow, garage + driveway, large south-facing garden)
properties.body: A two-bedroom semi-detached bungalow in a small quiet cul-de-sac in the Brixington area of Exmouth, in need of modernisation. The front door is to the side and opens into an L-shaped reception hall, with doors to two good-sized bedrooms, a bathroom/WC and a spacious living room with patio doors out to the rear garden; off the living room is a kitchen with a small enclosed rear porch. Gas central heating and extensive uPVC double glazing. Gardens front and rear, with a driveway leading to a garage, and the large rear garden faces south with a fine sunny aspect — the standout feature of the property. EPC E, Council Tax C, freehold, no chain. About two miles from the town centre and seafront, and a short walk from local shops, schools, bus routes and Brixington Park.
properties.why: A freehold bungalow in Exmouth with both a garage and a driveway, plus a large south-facing garden, and no chain. It clears the stairs question and the parking requirement cleanly. The reservation is value: at £275,000 for something explicitly needing modernisation and rated EPC E, this is the sort of listing Bro 3 reliably marks down as expensive for what it is once the refurbishment cost is added to the asking price.

parking.note: A driveway leading to a garage, with gardens to both front and rear.

properties.aiTake: Freehold Exmouth bungalow with garage, driveway, a large south-facing garden and no chain — but no character at all and priced at £275,000 while explicitly needing modernisation, which is the combination that reliably reads as poor value.

properties.title: Valley Way, Exmouth (2-bed detached bungalow, driveway + garage, private south-facing garden, no chain)

flags.text: DETACHED BUNGALOW — ALL ON ONE LEVEL

properties.body: A two-bedroom detached bungalow on Valley Way, Exmouth, requiring a programme of modernisation and refurbishment. A reception hall with a coats cupboard leads to a lounge/dining room of nearly 20ft overlooking the rear garden, with a fitted gas fire, and a kitchen/breakfast room of about 12ft by 12ft with a wall-mounted Worcester boiler and a door out to the garden. Two bedrooms, both facing front, the larger with a fitted double wardrobe, and a bathroom/WC with bath and Mira shower over. uPVC double glazed windows and gas central heating via a modern boiler. To the side is a driveway providing off-road parking and leading to a garage, with a lawned front garden; the rear garden faces south and the agent describes it as enjoying a high degree of privacy and seclusion. Freehold, no ongoing chain.
properties.why: Detached matters here — it's the one in this batch with a garden the agent actively describes as private and secluded, which lines up with Jesse's preference for somewhere a bit more removed rather than overlooked. Freehold, driveway and garage, single storey, no chain, and the boiler is already modern. Like Elizabeth Road it needs work, so the real cost is above the £265,000 asking price.

parking.note: A driveway to the side of the bungalow providing off-road parking and leading to a garage.

properties.aiTake: Detached freehold bungalow in Exmouth with driveway, garage and a genuinely private south-facing garden — strong on the practical checklist and on seclusion, but plain, and the £265,000 asking price sits on top of a full refurbishment.

properties.title: Elwyn Road, Exmouth (ground-floor 2-bed, both en-suite, gated allocated parking)

flags.text: GROUND FLOOR — ALL ON ONE LEVEL
HAS PARKING (allocated, secure gated residents’ area)

properties.body: A purpose-built ground-floor two-bedroom apartment in the "Avenues" area of Exmouth, guide £280,000–£300,000 through Your Move, reduced on 11/08/2026 and described as a motivated seller with no ongoing chain. Entry is via a security door with remote unlocking into a hallway with ample storage and a utility cupboard plumbed for a washing machine, with space for a tumble dryer and the manifold for the underfloor heating. The main room is a large open-plan lounge/dining area with a modern integrated kitchen and French doors opening onto its own planted patio. Both bedrooms are doubles and both have their own white en-suite shower rooms, and there is a further cloakroom/WC. Outside are maintained communal gardens, a communal bin store and a secure shared shed with an individual lockable unit per flat. Parking is an allocated space inside a secure residents’ area behind remote-controlled gates onto Elwyn Road. Tenure is share of freehold on a 125-year lease running from 24 February 2011 (about 110 years remaining); the service charge is 6.6% of the annual budget, currently around £157 a month or £1,892.81 a year, covering buildings insurance and all communal areas. Exmouth station is 0.84 miles away.
properties.why: Of everything on this list, this is one of the very few that answers the "what if stairs stop being an option" question outright rather than theoretically — it is genuinely ground floor, level throughout, with its own patio via French doors and a gated allocated parking space a few steps away. Two double bedrooms each with their own en-suite is unusual at this price and makes it work properly for guests or family staying. The Avenues is a good part of Exmouth, under a mile from the station and walkable to the seafront. The reservations are the money. £280,000 is not cheap for a flat, the £1,893 annual service charge is a real ongoing cost on top, and it is a modern purpose-built block with no character whatsoever — the opposite end of the spectrum from the thatched cottages Jesse actually gravitates towards. The share of freehold and the 110-year lease are both reassuring, and the seller being motivated after a reduction is worth testing with an offer.

parking.note: An allocated space within a secure residents’ parking area, accessed through remote-controlled gates onto Elwyn Road — about as good as parking gets on a flat, since it is both allocated and gated rather than an open communal free-for-all. There is also a secure shared shed with an individual lockable storage unit for this flat, which would take bikes.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Both bedrooms have their own en-suite shower room, plus a separate cloakroom — three WCs in a two-bed flat

properties.aiTake: The most genuinely step-free option on the list — ground floor, own patio, gated allocated parking, two en-suites and share of freehold — but £280,000 with a £1,893 service charge for a modern block with no character is a lot of money for very little soul.

properties.title: Vansittart Drive, Exmouth (2-bed end terrace, driveway, garden room, no chain)
properties.body: A two-double-bedroom end-of-terrace house on Vansittart Drive, guide £255,000 through Links Estate Agents, added on 11/08/2026 and the newest Exmouth listing in this sweep. Downstairs is a modern fitted cloakroom, a living room and an impressive kitchen/breakfast room with a granite breakfast bar; upstairs are two good-sized doubles, the principal with a large built-in wardrobe, plus a modern bathroom. Gas central heating and uPVC double glazing throughout. Outside there is a brick paved driveway giving off-road parking, an enclosed low-maintenance rear garden, a sun room/conservatory and — the feature Links push hardest — a garden room they suggest would work as a home office or hobby room. Freehold, council tax band B, no onward chain. Exmouth station is 1.6 miles away. This is a different property from the £249,950 Vansittart Drive house already on the list, and from the £290,000 one currently marketed by Your Move on the same road.
properties.why: The garden room is the reason to look twice. Jesse has consistently rated separate, finished outbuildings — workshop, studio, bike space — as a genuine plus rather than a nice-to-have, and Bro 3 said the same explicitly about the sheds at Haynes Cottages. Here you get one, plus a sun room, plus a driveway, plus a downstairs cloakroom that makes a future ground-floor adaptation considerably easier, all freehold and chain-free at £255,000. Against that: it is an unremarkable modern end-terrace with no character at all, in a residential pocket a mile and a half back from both the station and the seafront, and £255,000 is £85,000 above Jesse’s real target. It is the practical option rather than the interesting one — but it does the practical things properly.

parking.note: A brick paved driveway to the front provides off-road parking, described by Links as part of the property rather than shared. Vansittart Drive is a wide residential road with unrestricted kerbside space as well, so a second vehicle or visitors are not a problem here.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Detached garden room set up as a home office/hobby room, plus a separate sun room — two extra usable spaces beyond the house itself

properties.aiTake: Driveway, garden room, sun room and a downstairs cloakroom, freehold and chain-free — a lot of practical boxes ticked for £255,000, with the honest caveat that it is a plain modern terrace with no character and sits well above the £170k target.

properties.title: Egremont Road, Exmouth (3-bed period terrace, 200 yards from the station, no chain)
properties.body: A three-bedroom freehold terraced house on Egremont Road, guide £265,000 through Bradleys, added on 07/08/2026 and offered with no onward chain. The floorplan totals 896 sq ft over two floors, split almost exactly evenly: downstairs a lounge (11’8" x 10’8") with a feature fireplace, a separate dining room (13’1" x 11’8") and a 12’7" x 8’0" kitchen at the back; upstairs two doubles (12’5" x 10’8" and 13’1" x 9’5"), a small third bedroom (8’0" x 6’2") and the bathroom. Bradleys highlight the high ceilings and the feature fireplace as the character draw. Outside is an enclosed rear garden with a patio, lawn, shed and rear access. What stands out on the map is the location: Exmouth station is 0.22 miles away, which is about a four-minute walk, and the seafront and town centre are a similar distance in the other direction.
properties.why: Three bedrooms, freehold, period features and a garden, four minutes from the train station and about the same from the town centre, for £265,000 — on paper this is one of the better-value Exmouth houses to appear in a while, and it is the closest to a station of anything currently on the list. The high ceilings and fireplace give it more character than the usual Exmouth terrace, and the third bedroom, small as it is, makes it genuinely flexible. The problem is parking. Bradleys do not mention any, which on a road of this type means kerbside only, and Egremont Road sits inside the Exmouth residents’ permit zone — so a permit is likely available but a guaranteed space is not. Parking is a hard requirement for an ordinary house in this search, and this is an ordinary house. Weigh the station and the price against the near-certainty of circling the block on a summer evening.

parking.note: No off-road parking is mentioned anywhere on the listing, so this is kerbside only. The useful part is that Egremont Road falls inside the Exmouth residents’ parking permit scheme — Devon County Council approved it after consultation, and Egremont Road is named within the "colonies" area (Zone A), one of five Exmouth zones with resident, visitor, essential visitor, business, trade and blue badge permit types. A resident permit therefore gives priority to park in the immediate area, which is a real improvement on unrestricted free-for-all streets, but it is not a reserved bay and it is not a guaranteed space — demand near the station is high. Check the current permit cost and the household allocation limit with Devon County Council, and note that the rear access shown on the floorplan is pedestrian, not vehicular.

properties.aiTake: A genuinely well-located three-bed freehold with period features, a garden and the station four minutes away at a fair price — held back only by having no parking at all beyond a residents’ permit.

properties.title: Greenway, Woodbury (2-bed semi, freehold, shared driveway, no chain)
properties.body: A two-bedroom semi-detached house on Greenway in the middle of Woodbury, freehold at £300,000 through Bradleys and added on 08/08/2026. Bradleys describe it as immaculately presented: a spacious living/dining room with French doors onto the garden, a modern kitchen, two double bedrooms and a contemporary shower room. Outside is a private decked garden, useful storage, and shared driveway parking. Offered with no onward chain. Council tax band C. The nearest stations are Exton (2.0 miles) and Lympstone Commando (2.0 miles). This is the fourth Greenway property to come through the search — the others are the £265,000 cob cottage, the £265,000 semi and the Grade II listed one reduced to £275,000 — so it is worth comparing all four side by side before deciding anything.
properties.why: Woodbury keeps earning its place in this search: the brother is in the village, Woodbury Common and its mountain bike trails are effectively on the doorstep, and Exmouth is a ten-minute drive. This one is freehold, chain-free, has genuine off-road parking and is turnkey rather than a project, which is a rarer combination than it sounds at this end of the market. The catch is the price. At £300,000 it lands exactly on the ceiling and £130,000 above Jesse’s actual target, for a two-bedroom house with no particular character — a modern, well-presented semi rather than anything unusual. Bro 3’s most consistent complaint across this whole list is "too expensive for what it is", and a plain two-bed at the top of budget is squarely in the path of it. The decked garden and the village position are the arguments in its favour; the price is the argument against.

parking.note: Shared driveway parking is included in the sale. Worth clarifying with Bradleys how many spaces it gives in practice and whether they are allocated or first-come — "shared driveway" on a Woodbury semi usually means one space each, but the arrangement is worth confirming in writing, and Greenway itself is a narrow village road with limited on-street overflow.

properties.aiTake: Freehold, chain-free and parked, in the one village that scores best on family and mountain bike trails — but a plain modern two-bed sitting right on the £300k ceiling, which is a lot of money for what is being offered.

properties.title: High Street, Budleigh Salterton (2-bed flat, chain free, minutes from the beach)

flags.text: ALL ON ONE LEVEL (57.5 sq m)
A FEW MINUTES’ WALK TO THE BEACH
FLOOR LEVEL NOT STATED — ASK AGENT

properties.body: A two-bedroom apartment right on Budleigh Salterton High Street, listed chain-free at £175,000 through Purplebricks and added on 08/08/2026. The floorplan runs to 57.5 sq m (619 sq ft) on a single level: a hall with a useful entrance storage cupboard, a separate living room (14’8" x 9’2"), a 15’1" x 8’2" kitchen, two bedrooms (14’8" x 9’0" and 10’10" x 8’1") and a bathroom positioned between them. There are no stairs anywhere inside the flat itself. Tenure is leasehold with the lease running to 28/09/2130 — about 105 years remaining — and Rightmove reports no ground rent and no service charge review period, with the actual service charge figure not published on the listing. Council tax band B. What the listing does not say anywhere, in the description or the key features, is which floor the flat is on, and the floorplan carries no "Ground Floor" label. That matters a lot here, so it is the first question for the agent.
properties.why: This is one of the cheapest ways into Budleigh Salterton town centre that has appeared in months, and at £175,000 it sits close to Jesse’s real £170k target rather than the £300k ceiling. Everything is on one level, which is exactly the long-term shape he has said he wants, and the High Street position puts the pebble beach, the Jurassic Coast path and the whole run of independent shops within a few minutes on foot. It is also close to the Otterton brother. The two problems are real, though. There is no parking at all — Budleigh’s High Street has only limited, restricted on-street bays, so this would mean paying for a car park permit indefinitely. And the listing never states which floor it is on, which, given the single-level floorplan is otherwise ideal for the no-stairs test, is the difference between a genuinely accessible flat and one reached by two flights of communal stairs. Worth a phone call before anything else.

parking.note: No parking of any kind is included and the High Street itself has only limited, time-restricted on-street bays — not a realistic place to keep a car. The practical answer in Budleigh is a council car park permit: East Devon District Council sells permits for its designated car parks, and Rolle Mews (7 Fore Street, with EV charging) and the Station Road car parks are the closest to this address, both a few minutes’ walk. Lower Station Road is a short-stay car park with the use restriction lifted from 1 October to 31 March. Budget for an annual permit as a standing cost, and check with EDDC which of the Budleigh car parks currently allow all-day resident permit parking before committing — the short-stay ones are not a substitute for a driveway.

properties.aiTake: Cheap for central Budleigh, chain-free, and entirely on one level — but no parking, no garden, no outside space at all, and the listing never says which floor it is on, which undercuts the one thing that would otherwise make it stand out.

properties.title: Madeira Villas, Exmouth (2-bed freehold semi, tenanted at £870pcm)
properties.body: A red-brick two-bedroom semi-detached house on a corner plot in Madeira Villas, off Exeter Road in central Exmouth, on with Pennys at £150,000 freehold. The ground floor is a single dual-aspect lounge/dining room of 15'8" x 15'6" (narrowing to 9'2") with windows to front and side, running through to a compact 8'0" x 6'8" kitchen with a wall-mounted gas boiler and a door out to the rear. Upstairs are two bedrooms — 11'6" x 8'10" and 9'3" x 6'7" — and a bathroom/WC with bath, basin and WC. Outside is an enclosed courtyard garden with a rear pedestrian gate. Double glazed, gas central heating, EPC C. The key caveat is in the listing's own feature list: there is a sitting tenant paying £870 per calendar month, so this is being marketed as an investment rather than as a vacant home, and vacant possession would need to be negotiated as part of any offer. Update 18/08/2026: now being sold by traditional online auction with Pennys on 4 September 2026 at 11.30am, rather than by private treaty — the £150,000 figure is effectively a guide, and the sitting tenant at £870pcm remains in place.
properties.why: £150,000 for a freehold semi-detached house in Exmouth is the cheapest house — not flat, house — the sweep has turned up in central Exmouth, and it is barely a ten-minute walk from the town centre and Exmouth Community College. At that number it clears Jesse's real £170k target with room to spare, which matters more than the fact that it is a plain 1930s-ish brick semi with no particular character. The two real problems are parking and the tenant. There is no driveway; the corner plot is fenced right up to the pavement and Madeira Villas sits inside Devon County Council's Exmouth Residents Parking Zone D, so it is a permit-and-hope arrangement rather than a space of your own. And the £870pcm tenant means this is priced as a yield play — roughly 7% gross — which is likely why it is this cheap. If Jesse wanted to live in it he would be asking the agent for vacant possession on completion before anything else. Worth putting in front of the brothers precisely because the price is so far below everything else on the page.

parking.note: No driveway or garage — the corner plot is fenced to the pavement and the listing makes no mention of parking at all. Madeira Villas falls inside Devon County Council's Exmouth Residents Parking Zone D, where on-street bays are restricted 8am–8pm and residents buy an annual permit through Devon's MiPermit system (postcode + house number). That makes a space likely but not guaranteed, and permits do not reserve a specific bay. Photos of the street show cars parked nose-to-tail along the kerb, so competition is real. The nearest off-street alternative for a second car is the Imperial Road / Camperdown long-stay council car parks about ten minutes' walk away.

properties.aiTake: The cheapest freehold house in Exmouth the search has found — walkable to town and the station, but plain, tenanted at £870pcm, with only a courtyard garden and permit-scheme kerbside parking.

properties.title: Duke of Cornwall Close, Exmouth (2-bed freehold terrace, allocated space, no chain)
properties.linkLabel: onthemarket.com — Duke of Cornwall Close, Exmouth
properties.body: A two-bedroom freehold terraced house in Duke of Cornwall Close, off Hulham Road on the Brixington side of Exmouth, guided at £170,000 through Pennys with no ongoing chain. Downstairs is a 13'10" x 12'5" lounge with the staircase and an understairs recess, opening into a 12'5" x 8'4" kitchen/breakfast room with a breakfast bar, a modern Ideal gas boiler, and a door to the rear garden. Upstairs, bedroom one is 9'10" x 9'3" with a mirror-fronted built-in wardrobe, bedroom two is 12'8" x 6'4" narrowing to 5'1", and the bathroom has a bath with shower over and a linen cupboard. The rear garden is fully enclosed and laid out for low maintenance with decorative stone and a patio; the front is decorative stone with a path to the door. The agent is explicit that general refurbishment is required. EPC E, last assessed back in 2009 — worth a fresh one.
properties.why: This lands exactly on Jesse's real £170,000 target rather than his £300,000 ceiling, and it does the two boring things that usually get lost at that price: it is freehold, and it comes with an allocated parking space. Bassetts Farm Primary is 0.2 miles away and the Brixington precinct is walkable, so it is a properly functional bit of Exmouth. It is also completely characterless — a 1970s-ish estate terrace with stone-chipping gardens — which is the opposite of the thatched-cottage end of this list, and it needs work throughout, so budget for a kitchen, bathroom and probably rewiring on top. The upside of that is obvious: at £170k with refurb money still leaving change against the ceiling, it is one of the few entries where Bro 3's habit of adding the renovation cost to the asking price still ends up looking sensible rather than damning.

parking.note: The listing states plainly under Outside: "Located close by is an allocated parking space." So a space comes with the house, though it is in a nearby communal bay rather than a driveway at the door — worth asking the agent to point out exactly which bay and how far it is from the front door, and whether the allocation is on the title deeds or an informal estate arrangement.

properties.aiTake: Right on the £170k target, freehold, chain-free and with an allocated space — a genuinely sensible Exmouth buy, let down by needing full refurbishment and having no character whatsoever.

properties.title: Parkside Drive, Exmouth (2-bed semi-detached bungalow, driveway + garage, renovation project)
properties.body: A two-bedroom semi-detached bungalow on Parkside Drive (EX8 4LD) in the Brixington area of Exmouth, on with Fulfords at £260,000 freehold, council tax band C, with no onward chain. The accommodation is a living room, two double bedrooms, a shower room and a kitchen — all on one level — with driveway parking and a garage outside. The agent is straightforward that it is a renovation project: "clear scope to modernise throughout and tailor the layout and finishes to suit individual tastes." Brixington Precinct is on the doorstep for everyday shopping, with the Salterton Road supermarkets and retail parks a short drive and the town centre, beach and seafront easily reached. Important: Fulfords have published a Section 21 notice on the listing stating they have already received an offer of £240,000, and that any interested party must submit a higher offer in writing to the agent before exchange of contracts — so this one is live and moving, not sitting.
properties.why: The bungalow format is the thing here. It is the only new find this sweep that answers the long-term question outright — everything on one level, no stairs to design around later — and it does it while also having a driveway and a garage, which is the workshop/bike space Jesse keeps coming back to. Being chain-free and a blank renovation canvas means the layout can be reworked rather than inherited. Against that: £260,000 is well above Jesse's real £170k target and in the band where Bro 3's "too expensive for what it is" reflex fires hardest, especially for a plain post-war bungalow with no character on a Brixington estate a mile and a half back from the sea. And there is already £240,000 on the table with contracts not yet exchanged, so anyone interested is bidding against a live offer rather than starting a conversation. Genuinely useful, not romantic.

parking.note: Driveway parking plus a garage, both confirmed in the agent's own description of the property. Parkside Drive is a wide, unrestricted residential road on the Brixington estate, so overflow kerbside space for a second vehicle or visitors is not a problem either.

properties.aiTake: A chain-free Exmouth bungalow with driveway, garage and everything on one level — the best long-term-liveability answer this sweep — but characterless, needing full modernisation, and already carrying a £240,000 offer at a £260,000 ask.

properties.title: Fulford Way, Woodbury (3-bed mid-terrace, no chain, Woodbury Common on the doorstep)

flags.text: PARKING UNKNOWN — "NO WAITING AT ANY TIME" ON THIS ROAD

properties.body: A three-bedroom mid-terrace house on Fulford Way in Woodbury village, on with Fulfords at £275,000 (recently reduced) with no onward chain, council tax band C, EPC C. Entrance hall into a bright living room with understairs storage, a dining area to the rear, and a kitchen off it. Upstairs are two double bedrooms plus a versatile third that would work as a nursery, office or single, and a modern family bathroom. The rear garden is small and low-maintenance. Woodbury village centre — store, primary school, pubs and cafés — is a couple of minutes away, Woodbury Common's walking, cycling and riding routes start on the edge of the village, Exmouth and Budleigh Salterton are both a short drive, and Exeter is about eight miles. Note Fulfords charge the buyer a non-refundable AML fee once an offer is accepted. Tenure is listed as "ask agent" rather than stated.
properties.why: Location is the whole case for this one. Woodbury puts Jesse in the same village as one brother and drops him straight onto Woodbury Common for the mountain biking, with the coast fifteen minutes down the hill — it is the strongest "close to family" tick of anything new this sweep, and three bedrooms plus two bathrooms is more usable space than most of the cottages on this page. The problems are parking and price. The listing does not mention parking at all, the cover photo shows a pedestrian path and lawn rather than a driveway, and Devon County Council confirmed a "No Waiting At Any Time" order along Fulford Way and Globe Hill in July 2024 — so kerbside parking outside the house is not legal, and where residents actually put cars needs establishing before anything else. On top of that £275,000 for a plain modern terrace, in a village where Bro 3 already marked down Globe Hill at £6/10 for being "a bit expensive for being away from the station and all", is exactly the shape of listing he tends to score in the fours.

parking.note: The listing does not mention parking anywhere, and the exterior photo shows a footpath and lawn frontage with no driveway. Worse, Devon County Council's July 2024 traffic order for East Devon confirmed "No Waiting At Any Time" on Fulford Way and Globe Hill in Woodbury — so parking directly outside is prohibited. Woodbury has no residents' permit scheme to fall back on, and the village's public parking is limited to a small free car park by the village hall / Woodbury Village Stores plus informal spaces near the church, none of it intended as overnight residents' parking. Estates of this era in Woodbury often have a shared parking court set back from the road, which is the most likely answer here, but nothing in the listing or photos confirms one. Treat this as the first question for the agent: is a parking space or court bay included, and is it on the title?

properties.aiTake: Right village — brother nearby, Woodbury Common on the doorstep — and three beds with two bathrooms, but plain, £275,000, tenure unstated, and no parking mentioned on a road that now carries a No Waiting At Any Time order.

properties.title: Meadow Road, Budleigh Salterton (ground-floor 2-bed flat with its own private garden — AUCTION)
properties.price: Guide Price from £155,000 (modern method of auction)

flags.text: ⚠ DEVON OCCUPANCY RESTRICTION — 3-YEAR LOCAL CONNECTION REQUIRED
GROUND FLOOR — ALL ON ONE LEVEL
OWN PRIVATE ENCLOSED REAR GARDEN + STORE
MODERN METHOD OF AUCTION — RESERVATION FEE ON TOP
LEASEHOLD — ~99 YRS LEFT, £10 GROUND RENT, £224/YR SERVICE CHARGE

properties.body: A purpose-built ground-floor two-double-bedroom flat on Meadow Road, about half a mile from Budleigh Salterton's town centre and seafront, offered for sale by modern method of auction through iamsold with a guide from £155,000 plus a reservation fee (quote reference RB0167). Accommodation is all on one level: hall, a bright lounge opening into a small conservatory with underfloor heating that looks over the garden, a dual-aspect fitted kitchen, two double bedrooms (10'6" x 8'6" and 9'10" x 8'6") and a modern white bathroom suite. The property has been recently redecorated and well maintained, with a new Worcester Bosch gas combi boiler and new uPVC double glazing, soffits, fascias and guttering. Outside it has its own good-sized fully enclosed private rear garden, mainly lawn, with a gated side entrance and a lockable private garden store. Council tax band A. Leasehold, running from 19/04/2000 to 11/04/2125 — around 99 years remaining — with ground rent of £10 a year and a service charge of £224 a year. Vacant possession, no onward chain. Critically, a Devon Occupancy Restriction applies: the buyer must have lived or worked in Devon (or a combination of the two) for three years.
properties.why: On paper this is one of the better-value things on the whole page. £155,000 buys a genuinely ground-floor two-double-bedroom home half a mile from the beach in Budleigh, with its own private enclosed garden and a lockable store — not a shared communal lawn, an actual garden — plus a nearly-new boiler and windows, so nothing needs spending on day one. It answers the long-term stairs question completely, and the lease is a comfortable 99 years with a trivial £10 ground rent and a £224 service charge. Two things need eyes on before getting excited. First, the Devon Occupancy Restriction: the buyer must have lived or worked in Devon for three years, which is a real gate for someone moving in from outside the county and needs checking against Jesse's own circumstances before any bid — it is also the likeliest reason the guide price is this low. Second, it is a modern-method auction, so there is a non-refundable reservation fee on top of the guide and a fixed timetable once reserved. Parking is kerbside only. Even with all that, a ground-floor flat with a private garden in Budleigh at £155k earns its place on the list.

parking.note: The agent's own notes say simply "On-road parking" — there is no allocated bay, driveway or garage. The good news is that Budleigh Salterton has no residents' permit scheme, and Meadow Road is a quiet unrestricted residential road about half a mile back from the seafront, so kerbside space outside or near the flat is realistic year-round rather than only out of season. The flat also has a gated side entrance and a lockable garden store, which handles bike storage without needing a garage. For a second vehicle or visitors in high summer, East Devon District Council's Lime Kiln, Rolle Mews and Brook Road car parks are all in the town centre roughly ten minutes' walk away, with annual resident season tickets available.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A Devon Occupancy Restriction on the title — the buyer must have lived or worked in Devon for three years, which is unusual outside new-build local-needs housing and is almost certainly what is holding the guide price down.

properties.aiTake: Cheap, chain-free, genuinely ground-floor and with its own private garden and store half a mile from Budleigh beach — held back by a three-year Devon residency restriction, auction fees, kerbside-only parking and a 99-year lease.

properties.title: Byron Way, Exmouth (2-bed terrace, private driveway + garage, no chain)
properties.body: A two-double-bedroom terraced house in the Brixington area of Exmouth, chain-free at £239,950 through Pennys. Ground floor is a 15'6" lounge with stairs and understairs cupboard, opening into an 11'9" kitchen/dining room with patio doors onto the garden. Upstairs are two bedrooms (11'9" x 9'1" and 11'9" x 7'2") and a bathroom/WC with a Mira shower over the bath. The garden runs to a southerly aspect with patio, a sun terrace under a canopy, and an octagonal summer house. The standout is outside: a private driveway leading to a 17'5" x 8'10" garage with an up-and-over door, plus a strip of lawn beside the garage the agent suggests could become further storage. Pennys have not stated the tenure on the listing and Rightmove is showing their standard "please confirm freehold or leasehold" prompt, so that is a first question for the agent.
properties.why: This is the practical end of the search rather than the romantic end, but it does the practical things unusually well for the money. A private driveway *and* a full-size garage on a terraced house is genuinely rare — most of the Brixington terraces have nothing but kerbside — and that 17-foot garage is the workshop/bike-storage space Jesse has consistently wanted, with the summer house as a second usable outbuilding on top. A south-facing enclosed garden and no onward chain add to it. The honest caveats: it is a plain post-war terrace with no character at all, which is the thing Jesse actually cares most about, and Brixington sits a mile and a half back from the seafront rather than on it. Woodbury Common is an easy ride out from this side of town, which helps. At £239,950 it is priced fairly rather than cheaply, so expect Bro 3 to weigh the garage against his usual "boring for the money" test.

parking.note: A private driveway leading to its own 17'5" x 8'10" garage with up-and-over door — the agent calls it "a superb feature and unique point to this property", which is fair, since most of the surrounding Byron Way terraces have no off-road parking at all. There is also a lawned strip beside the garage that could take a second vehicle or become storage.

properties.aiTake: A plain but well-equipped Exmouth terrace whose real draw is a private driveway plus a full 17ft garage and a south-facing garden with a summer house — strong on workshop space and parking, chain-free, but with zero character and an unstated tenure to check.

properties.title: Cranford Avenue, Exmouth (ground-floor 2-bed flat with garage — short lease)

flags.text: GROUND FLOOR — ALL ON ONE LEVEL
HAS PARKING (single garage in nearby block)
LEASEHOLD — ONLY ~42 YRS LEFT (below the 80-yr threshold)

properties.body: A ground-floor two-double-bedroom apartment on Cranford Avenue, reached by its own private front door off the communal hallway. The rooms are generous for the price: a 15'11" x 12'3" lounge/dining room with a door onto a covered sun terrace that opens directly onto the communal gardens, an 11'3" kitchen, a 16'7" principal bedroom and an 11' second bedroom, both with fitted floor-to-ceiling wardrobes, plus a bathroom/WC. A single garage in a nearby block with an up-and-over door comes with it, and the development has extensive, well-maintained communal lawns and mature planting front and rear. Two things explain the £150,000 asking price, and Pennys are upfront about both: the flat needs a full programme of modernisation and refurbishment, and — in their words — "price reflects length of lease". The lease is 99 years from 1969, so roughly 42 years remain. Service charge is £1,530.87 for 2025 (revised annually) and ground rent is £10 every six months.
properties.why: On the face of it this hits several things at once that rarely come together: genuinely cheap, explicitly ground floor with no internal stairs at all, two proper double bedrooms rather than a double and a box room, its own garage, and mature communal gardens right outside the sun terrace. For the "could still live here if stairs became a problem" test it is the strongest kind of answer — it is already all on one level. The problem is the lease, and it is a serious one rather than a technicality. At around 42 years remaining it is well under the 80-year mark where marriage value kicks in, which means most mainstream lenders will not touch it without an extension, and extending will cost a meaningful five-figure sum on top of the purchase price and legal fees. Add a full refurbishment and a £1,531 annual service charge and the true all-in cost lands a long way above the £150,000 headline — quite possibly north of £220,000 for a flat with no character. Worth a conversation with the agent about whether the freeholder will grant an extension and at what price, because that single answer decides whether this is a bargain or a trap. Bro 3 has already said he is wary of anything not comfortably over 100 years, so expect a low score from him.

parking.note: A single garage with an up-and-over door in a nearby block is included with the flat, so off-road parking is secured and there is lock-up storage for bikes. Worth confirming with Pennys whether the garage is demised under the same lease as the flat (and therefore subject to the same ~42-year term) or held separately, since that affects both the extension cost and what a lender will accept.

properties.aiTake: Cheap, properly all-on-one-level, two real doubles and its own garage — but a ~42-year lease puts it below the mortgageable threshold and the extension plus a full refurbishment would push the true cost far past the £150,000 headline.

properties.title: Meadow View Road, Exmouth (modernised 3-bed end terrace, integrated garage)

flags.text: HAS PARKING (integrated garage + ample off-road parking)

properties.body: A freehold three-bedroom end-of-terrace house on Meadow View Road, recently modernised throughout by the current owners and offered at £270,000 through Fulfords. The ground floor opens into a large kitchen with extensive worktop and cupboard space and an integrated oven and hob, leading through to a refurbished living room with new flooring and French doors onto the garden. Upstairs are three bedrooms — two generous doubles with fitted wardrobes and a third good-sized single suited to a nursery, office or guest room — plus a fully renovated family bathroom with an L-shaped bath and shower over, and a landing linen cupboard with its own radiator. The rear garden has been landscaped with a large patio for dining and a separate fenced section laid with artificial grass. Side access leads round to ample off-road parking at the front. The integrated garage houses the boiler and consumer unit and has power, water and plumbing for a washing machine already run to it. The agent also flags scope for a side extension, subject to planning.
properties.why: This is the most turn-key thing in the search right now: freehold, three bedrooms, fully modernised so there is nothing that has to be done on day one, and parking sorted twice over with both an integrated garage and off-road space at the front. The garage is more interesting than the usual empty single: it already has power, water and plumbing run into it, which makes it a credible workshop straight away and — combined with the flagged side-extension scope — an unusually realistic route to a downstairs bedroom and shower room later, which is exactly the long-term adaptability question Jesse keeps coming back to. Against that, it is a modern estate house with no character whatsoever, it sits back from the seafront in the Withycombe/Brixington part of town rather than anywhere with a view, and at £270,000 it is in the upper third of the budget for something that is comfortable rather than special. Woodbury Common is handy from this side of Exmouth and both brothers are a short drive away. It scores as a sensible option rather than an exciting one.

parking.note: Ample off-road parking on the frontage plus an integrated garage, reached by a side access path from the rear garden. The garage is a working utility space rather than just storage — it houses the boiler and consumer unit and already has power, water and washing-machine plumbing connected.

properties.aiTake: Freehold, fully modernised, three bedrooms, off-road parking plus an integrated garage already wired and plumbed as a workshop — practically the strongest package here, marked down for having no character and sitting near the top of the budget.

properties.title: Land parcels, Exmouth Road, Ebford/Exton (⅓ acre — AUCTION)
properties.body: Freehold parcels of land, each about a third of an acre (roughly 13,000 sq ft / 1,208 sq m), on the Exmouth Road between the villages of Ebford and Exton, offered by auction with a £30,000 guide. The listing describes a prominent roadside position with established vehicle access. Critically, this is bare land with no planning permission — the agent markets it as "ideal for a variety of uses subject to the necessary consents" and it carries a 30% planning overage, meaning if residential or other valuable consent is ever obtained, 30% of the resulting uplift in value is payable back to the seller. Reserve is set within the guide range or no more than 10% above it, and the usual auction fees apply on top. Came to market 2 August 2026. Update 18/08/2026: the auction date is now confirmed — the individual parcels (Plots C and D, each about 0.3 acres, EX3 0PQ) are listed by Auction House South West for National Online Auction starting 1 September 2026 and ending 2 September 2026, each at a £30,000 guide plus fees, still freehold and still subject to the planning overage.
properties.why: Worth tracking because it is cheap, genuinely unconventional, and in a spot that suits Jesse well on paper — the Ebford/Exton stretch sits right by the Exe estuary with Exton station on the Avocet line, ten minutes from Exmouth and very close to the Woodbury brother, with Woodbury Common trails a short ride away. At £30,000 the downside is small in absolute terms. But it should be read as a speculative punt rather than a route to a home, and the reasons are stacked up in the listing itself. There is no planning permission of any kind, this is open countryside outside any settlement boundary, and East Devon is not in the habit of granting new isolated dwellings there. The 30% overage clause is the clearest signal of all: the seller has priced in the possibility that a buyer tries for consent, and has arranged to take almost a third of the gain if it ever lands. Note also that Plot B on the same stretch of Exmouth Road, tracked here separately, went to auction on 3 August 2026 with a £75,000 guide and its listing has now been pulled — so this may well be the same land being re-marketed at a lower guide, which is a fact worth establishing with the agent before bidding.

parking.note: The listing specifically calls out a prominent roadside position with established vehicle access, so the parcel can be driven onto directly from the Exmouth Road rather than needing a right of way negotiated over someone else's land — which is the single most valuable practical attribute bare land of this kind can have. There is nothing built, so any actual hardstanding or driveway would be the buyer's to create, subject to consent.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A third of an acre of freehold Devon countryside between the estuary and Woodbury Common, with its own roadside vehicle access, for the price of a car.

properties.aiTake: A third of an acre with its own road access, ten minutes from Exmouth and next to Woodbury Common, for £30,000 — but it is bare countryside with no planning permission and a 30% overage clause, so it is a cheap speculative punt on consent rather than anywhere to live.

research.question: Sweep re-check — auction timing and how the parcels are being offered.
research.findings: Confirmed live and imminent. Auction House South West is running this as a National Online Auction opening 1 September 2026 and ending 24 hours later on 2 September — five days from this sweep. The land is being offered as individually numbered parcels rather than one block: Plot C (Rightmove 92086383) and Plot D (Rightmove 92086401) are each listed separately at a £30,000 guide, each about 0.3 acres, both freehold with established vehicular access from the A376. The auctioneer confirms the planning overage provision applies, with full terms in the free legal pack. Still bare land with no planning permission, so the overage only bites if consent is ever obtained.

properties.title: Raleigh Road, Ottery St Mary (2-bed bungalow, garage with power)
properties.linkLabel: rightmove.co.uk — Raleigh Road, Ottery St Mary
properties.body: A freehold two-bedroom semi-detached bungalow on the eastern outskirts of Ottery St Mary at £250,000, a level walk from the town centre. Accommodation is a reception porch and hall, a fully fitted kitchen with built-in oven and gas hob and slate-effect worktops, a sitting/dining room with a large picture window and a feature fireplace, two double bedrooms both with built-in wardrobes, and a modern shower room. uPVC double glazing throughout, gas central heating and a new gas boiler. Outside there is a driveway giving off-road parking and access to a garage fitted with a remote-operated electric door, light, power and a utility area at one end. The front garden is open-plan lawn; the rear is fully enclosed, mainly paved for low maintenance, with established flowerbeds and a large timber shed which the agent suggests would suit conversion to a home office or summer house.
properties.why: This is the most straightforwardly practical entry of the batch and it ticks the two boxes that are hardest to find together: it is a bungalow, so the stay-put-if-stairs-become-a-problem question is answered outright rather than as an adaptation, and the garage has light, power and a utility area, which makes it a usable workspace rather than just somewhere to put a car. Add a driveway on top, a new boiler, an enclosed low-maintenance garden and a shed with home-office potential, and there is very little that would need spending on straight away. The case against is the one Jesse and Bro 3 both apply hardest. There is no character here — it is a mid-century estate bungalow, competently presented, with nothing unusual about it — and Ottery St Mary is properly inland, roughly 25 minutes from the nearest sea and about the same again from Exmouth, so it fails both the ocean and the close-to-family tests. At £250,000 for two bedrooms it also sits in exactly the zone where Bro 3 has repeatedly said a place feels expensive for what it is.

parking.note: A private driveway to the front giving off-road parking, leading to a garage with a remote-operated electric door, light and power, and a utility area built into one end — so both a parked car and a working garage, not one at the expense of the other.

properties.aiTake: Ticks the practical boxes cleanly — a true bungalow, a driveway, and a garage with power and a utility that would actually work as a workshop — but it has no character at all and sits inland, well away from both the sea and either brother.

properties.title: Salterton Road, Exmouth (3-bed period apartment, all on one level)

flags.text: ALL ON ONE LEVEL (84.3 sq m)

properties.body: A three-bedroom apartment in a substantial red-brick-and-render Victorian villa on Salterton Road, at £300,000 with off-road parking. The floorplan shows 84.3 sq m (908 sq ft) laid out entirely on one level: a long central hall running the depth of the apartment, a 6.00m x 4.27m living room with a bay window, kitchen, three bedrooms (the principal at 4.54m x 2.68m with an en-suite shower room) and a separate family bathroom. The listing emphasises high ceilings, decorative ceiling details and a lot of natural light, and the photographs bear that out. The building itself is handsome, with a two-storey canted bay, brick quoining and a lawned frontage. Two things the listing does not state: which floor of the building the apartment occupies, and the tenure — Rightmove records tenure as "ask agent", with no lease length given. Checked specifically and confirmed it is neither retirement/age-restricted nor shared ownership.
properties.why: Of everything found this sweep, this has the most actual period character combined with a genuinely useful layout — 908 sq ft of three-bedroom accommodation, all on a single level, in a proper Victorian villa, with off-road parking on a road that runs toward the seafront. Single-level living at this size is the thing worth noting: if it turns out to be the ground-floor apartment, it answers the stay-put-long-term question outright rather than conditionally. The problem is that two of the most important facts are missing from the listing. The tenure is simply not stated, and for an apartment that matters enormously — a short lease would change the picture completely, and Bro 3 has already marked one property down hard for exactly this kind of ambiguity. The floor level is also unstated, and while the ground-floor bay in the photographs matches the bay on the plan, the building has a matching bay at first-floor level too, so it cannot be settled from the pictures. Both are single questions to the agent. Beyond that it sits right on the £300,000 ceiling, has no private garden, and is on a main road rather than the quiet or rural setting Jesse has said he leans towards.

parking.note: The listing states off-road parking is included, and the photographs show a gravelled and paved parking area to the side of the building, reached down the drive past the lawn. What is not specified is whether that is an allocated numbered space or shared among the flats in the building — worth asking, since Salterton Road itself is a busy through route where on-street parking would be a poor fallback.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A three-bedroom, 908 sq ft apartment laid out entirely on one level inside a Victorian villa — the space of a house with none of the stairs, which is an unusual combination at this price.

properties.aiTake: The most genuine period character of this batch, with 908 sq ft of three-bed accommodation all on one level and off-road parking in Exmouth — but it sits right on the budget ceiling with no garden, and the listing states neither the tenure nor which floor it is on, which are exactly the two facts that would decide it.

properties.title: All Saints Mews, Exmouth (3-bed freehold townhouse, no chain)
properties.body: A freehold three-double-bedroom townhouse arranged over three floors in a small mews off All Saints, offered chain-free at £270,000 and a level walk from Exmouth town centre, the railway station and the bus interchange. Ground floor: entrance hall, utility room and bedroom three. First floor: lounge/dining room, kitchen and bathroom/WC. Second floor: the master and bedroom two. The garage has been split to create that third bedroom plus a lockable store, and the agent explicitly states it "could be reverted to the original full size garage" — so a buyer can choose between three bedrooms or a full garage plus two. To the rear is a small enclosed courtyard garden looking towards All Saints Church.
