properties.why: On the practical criteria this is one of the tidier packages in Exmouth itself: freehold rather than leasehold, three double bedrooms, no chain, its own garage, and close enough to the station and the seafront to tick coast, train and family-proximity all at once. The reversible garage conversion is genuinely useful optionality — keep bedroom three, or take the garage back for a workshop, which is the sort of flexibility most terraces at this price do not offer. The ground-floor bedroom also gives a partial head start on staying put long-term, though the bathroom is a floor above it, so a downstairs WC or shower would still be needed to make that work properly. Where it loses ground is character: this is a modern mews house over three floors, not a cottage, and Jesse has been consistent that he would rather have something with a story to it. At £270,000 it also sits in the band where Bro 3's "expensive for what it is" reflex tends to fire, particularly for a house with only a courtyard rather than a garden.

parking.note: A garage belonging to the property, currently divided into bedroom three and a lockable store, which the agent states can be reverted to its original full size — so off-road parking is included in the title either way, it is just a question of whether the buyer wants the space as a bedroom or as a garage.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A garage deliberately converted into a bedroom-plus-store that the agent confirms can be turned straight back into a full garage — rare flexibility to swap a room for a workshop and back again.

properties.aiTake: Freehold, chain-free, three doubles, a reversible garage and a level walk to both the station and the sea — a genuinely practical Exmouth buy that is marked down mainly for being a modern mews house with a courtyard rather than the characterful cottage Jesse actually wants.

properties.title: Single Building Plot, Core Hill Road, Sidmouth (self-build, full planning granted)

flags.text: BUILD COST ON TOP OF PLOT PRICE

properties.body: A freehold single building plot of about 0.126 acres (0.05 ha) on the north-western edge of Sidmouth, north of Woolbrook Mead and close to the Waitrose. Detailed — not outline — planning permission was granted by East Devon District Council under reference 23/2134/FUL on 5 February 2024 for the construction of one new detached dwelling and associated works. The approved design is a three-bedroom dormer-style house of roughly 191 sq m (2,063 sq ft): ground floor gives an entrance hall, an en-suite bedroom, utility, WC and an open-plan kitchen/living/dining room opening onto the garden; the upper floor adds two large bedrooms, both en-suite with built-in wardrobes. Off-road parking is shown at the front, accessed from Core Hill Road, with an established westerly-facing garden to the rear. The lead photo is an aerial with the plot boundary drawn on it, which places it clearly in an established residential area with the sea visible in the distance.
properties.why: Jesse has asked repeatedly for self-build plots to be surfaced, and this is the strongest version of that this sweep found: the hard planning risk is already retired, because permission is detailed rather than outline and covers a specific approved house, so a buyer is not gambling on whether East Devon will ever allow a dwelling here. The approved layout is also unusually well-suited to him without needing any redesign — there is a full en-suite bedroom, utility and WC on the ground floor alongside the living space, which is the ground-floor-forever box ticked from day one rather than as a later adaptation. Two real caveats. First, £220,000 buys the land only; a 191 sq m house will realistically cost well north of £250,000 to build, so the all-in figure lands far above the £300,000 ceiling even though the listing price sits under it. Second, a February 2024 detailed consent carries the standard three-year commencement window, so it expires around February 2027 unless work has lawfully started — worth confirming with EDDC before doing anything else. Location-wise Sidmouth is about 30 minutes from Exmouth and 20 from Otterton, so it is the weakest of this batch on closeness to family, and there is no railway station in the town at all.

parking.note: The approved scheme includes off-road parking at the front of the plot, accessed directly off Core Hill Road — so parking comes as part of the planning permission rather than being something to negotiate later. Because nothing is built yet, the exact number of spaces follows whatever the approved site plan shows; worth pulling the drawings from the East Devon planning portal under 23/2134/FUL to confirm the count before committing.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A blank slate with the planning fight already won — detailed consent for a specific 2,063 sq ft three-bed house, so the design can be built as approved or varied, rather than starting from an outline permission and hoping.

properties.aiTake: The self-build option Jesse keeps asking for, with detailed planning already granted and a ground-floor en-suite bedroom in the approved layout — but £220,000 is the land alone, and the build cost on top pushes the real total well past the ceiling, in a town that is the furthest of this batch from both brothers.

properties.title: Station Road, Broadclyst (period cottage with a 25ft workshop)
properties.body: A two-bedroom terraced period cottage in the middle of Broadclyst, guided at £220,000–£230,000 and freehold. The floorplan is the interesting part: the ground floor is porch, living room, kitchen and — unusually for a cottage this size — a shower room, with the two bedrooms upstairs. Total floor area including outbuildings is 104.8 sq m. Outside is an enclosed rear garden and a genuinely substantial run of outbuildings: a workshop measuring 7.85m x 2.13m (25'9" x 7'0"), a utility/shed, a shed fitted out as a home office, and a summer house. All four appear on the floorplan and, importantly, are photographed — the summer house is fully timber-lined with a woodburner and full-height glazing, and the workshop/store is a proper lined building rather than a flat-pack shed. Parking is on-street only. Broadclyst is a National Trust estate village on the edge of Ashclyst Forest, one of the larger blocks of woodland in East Devon.
properties.why: This is the closest thing this sweep found to the character-plus-workshop combination Jesse keeps circling, at a price inside his real target range rather than at the ceiling. A 25-foot workshop, a home-office shed and a woodburner-fitted summer house is a lot of usable outbuilding for £220,000, and the downstairs shower room already existing means converting the living room to a bedroom later is a realistic route to staying put long-term rather than a hopeful guess. Bro 3 has previously marked a property down for claiming a barn it never photographed — that objection does not apply here, every outbuilding is both drawn on the plan and shown in the gallery. The honest arguments against are all about location: Broadclyst is properly inland with no sea, it is roughly 25-30 minutes from Exmouth and further from Otterton, so it fails the close-to-family test on both counts, and parking is on-street only. Ashclyst Forest on the doorstep does at least answer the trails question, just not with Woodbury Common.

parking.note: The listing says only "on-street parking is available nearby", with no driveway, garage or allocated space — and the floorplan confirms the outbuildings occupy the rear, so there is no scope to create off-road parking without losing the workshop. Broadclyst is a National Trust estate village with no residents' permit scheme and no public car park of any size; the practical options are the unrestricted stretches of Station Road and the surrounding lanes, plus the village hall and school areas which fill on weekdays. Free and unmetered, but genuinely first-come-first-served, and the terrace fronts more or less straight onto the road, so a space directly outside is not something to count on.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A fully timber-lined summer house with its own woodburner, alongside a separate 25ft workshop and a shed fitted out as a home office — and unlike most listings making outbuilding claims, all of them are photographed and drawn on the floorplan.

properties.aiTake: Real period character, a freehold title, a downstairs shower room and about 40 feet of genuinely photographed workshop and summer house for £220,000 — held back from a higher score purely by geography, being inland with no coast and a good half-hour from both brothers.

properties.title: Talaton, EX5 2RG (Grade II thatched cottage)
properties.body: A properly thatched Grade II listed cottage in the middle of Talaton, a few steps from the village green, offered with no onward chain. Ground floor: a cosy sitting room with a striking stone inglenook fireplace, a leaded-light window with a window seat and an abundance of exposed ceiling beams; a kitchen with wall and base units, built-in oven, hob and extractor and an integrated washing machine; and a couple of steps down to a dining area with wooden flooring and more beams, which opens directly into Bedroom Two and on to a rear porch and the garden. First floor: the principal bedroom with built-in storage, plus the bathroom. Heating is electric storage heaters — mains gas is not connected. Council Tax Band C, freehold, EPC-exempt as a listed building. Outside there is a rear garden mostly laid to lawn with a flowerbed and a summerhouse; separately, the current owner and the neighbours rent an adjoining strip of garden land from a local landowner for a modest annual sum, and the landowner has indicated they are happy for that to continue — worth confirming in writing, since it is rented rather than owned. The village itself has a community-run shop and post office, a pub, an active village hall and a medieval parish church; Ottery St Mary is 3 miles away, Honiton 5 miles with a train station, and the A30 is close for Exeter and the M5.
properties.why: This is the best straight-up thatched cottage the sweep has turned up in budget for a while — genuinely thatched, genuinely Grade II, freehold, chain-free, with a stone inglenook, beams throughout and a garden with a summerhouse, all at £245,000 rather than the £385,000–£450,000 the East Budleigh and Castle Lane thatched cottages want. It also gives Jesse a downstairs room already being used as a bedroom. The honest trade-off is geography: Talaton is inland, about 25 minutes from the Budleigh/Sidmouth coast and roughly 20 minutes from both brothers rather than the few miles the East Budleigh options manage, and it has no parking of its own. Electric storage heating and the rented garden strip are two more things to price in.

parking.note: The listing says nothing at all about parking for the cottage — no driveway, garage or allocated space is mentioned, and the only parking reference in the whole description is to the "unreserved parking" at the parish church, which is a general village amenity rather than anything attached to this property. Researching it: Talaton has no residents' permit scheme and no council car park at all — Devon County Council handles on-street parking countywide and East Devon District Council's car parks are all in the towns (Ottery St Mary, Honiton, Budleigh, Exmouth), none in the village. In practice that means unrestricted on-street/verge parking on the lanes around the green, plus the church and village hall car parks which are informally used by residents. That is usually workable in a village this small, but it is not guaranteed and it is not the same as owning a space — worth asking Redferns directly whether the cottage has any recognised parking right, because for a listed cottage in a conservation-sensitive village there is no realistic prospect of creating a driveway.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Full thatched roof, stone inglenook fireplace and leaded-light window with a window seat — plus an adjoining strip of garden land rented annually from a neighbouring landowner

properties.aiTake: A real thatched Grade II cottage — inglenook, beams, summerhouse garden, freehold and chain-free — at £245,000, which is a lot of character per pound; it loses points for being genuinely inland (no sea, ~20 minutes from either brother) and for having no parking of its own.

properties.title: Station Road, Budleigh Salterton (ground-floor Edwardian conversion)

flags.text: SHARE OF FREEHOLD (lease to be created on completion)

properties.body: A spacious ground-floor apartment forming part of a distinctive Edwardian town house on Station Road, right beside The Green in Budleigh Salterton. 796 sq ft on one level: lounge/diner, kitchen/breakfast room, two double bedrooms, bathroom, and generous storage throughout. The agent's line is that the building has "managed to retain a great deal of character and charm", and the conversion has kept the period proportions rather than chopping them up. There is a communal front garden included. EPC C. Tenure is a share of freehold, to be created on completion — so the exact lease length isn't stated yet and needs pinning down with the solicitor. Pets and lettings are both permitted. Notably it is available for the first time in 21 years. Walking distance to the town's shops, the seafront and the bus routes; Exmouth and its train station are about five miles away.
properties.why: On paper this ticks more of Jesse's actual long-term boxes than almost anything else at this price: it is fully ground floor with two double bedrooms, so the "could I still live here if I couldn't manage stairs" test is already passed rather than merely adaptable; it is in Budleigh Salterton a few minutes' walk from the sea; it is a period conversion rather than a modern box; and at £189,950 it sits below Jesse's real £170k–£200k comfort zone rather than at the £300k ceiling. It is also close to both brothers — Otterton is about three miles, Woodbury about six. The gaps are parking, which the listing simply doesn't address, and the share-of-freehold structure needing proper legal checking because the lease is only being created at completion.

parking.note: The listing makes no mention of parking at all — no allocated space, garage or driveway is claimed, and the photos don't show one. Researching the street specifically: Station Road is where East Devon District Council's Lower Station Road car park sits, effectively on the doorstep, and EDDC's published rules give it no restriction of use at all between 1 October and 31 March, which makes winter parking straightforward and free. Outside that window it is a paid short-stay car park, but EDDC sells virtual monthly permits at £10/month for one town (Budleigh Salterton is one of the eligible towns), rising in £2 steps if you want to add more towns, with no physical permit to display. So the realistic position is: no parking with the flat, but a council car park within yards of the front door and a cheap monthly permit that covers it — a better fallback than most of the no-parking cottages on this list. Still worth asking David Rhys & Co whether any of the building's residents have an informal arrangement, because a converted Edwardian town house of this size often has some rear access.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Part of a distinctive Edwardian town house beside The Green, on the market for the first time in 21 years

properties.aiTake: Fully ground-floor, two doubles, period character, five minutes from the Budleigh seafront and close to both brothers, at £189,950 — the ground-floor-for-life test is passed outright; the catches are no parking of its own (though the council car park is on the same street) and a share-of-freehold lease that only gets written at completion.

properties.title: Rock Cottages, Alfington (2-bed cottage with carport)

flags.text: NIGHT STORAGE HEATING / SHARED PRIVATE DRAINAGE

properties.body: A two-bedroom mid-terrace cottage in the hamlet of Alfington, offered with no onward chain at a £185,000 guide. Ground floor: a lounge with a feature fireplace and wood-burning fire, a separate dining room, and a kitchen with base units and built-in appliances. First floor: two bedrooms and a shower room. Described by the agent as beautifully presented. Crucially for this list it has genuine off-road parking — a 4.18m x 2.58m carport — which almost nothing else at this price in a village setting does. Rear access leads to a brick-paved patio and an artificial-lawned garden with a pergola, all landscaped. Two practical caveats stated in the listing: heating is night storage heaters, not gas central heating, and drainage is shared private drainage rather than mains. The front elevation is rendered and fronts straight onto the lane, and the render on the plinth looks tired in the photos even though the interior is smart. Alfington sits just outside Ottery St Mary with A30 access and a bus service.
properties.why: It is one of the cheapest genuinely rural, genuinely characterful cottages the sweep has found that also comes with its own off-road parking — that combination is rare enough to be worth tracking on its own. At £185,000 it lands inside Jesse's real target range rather than near the ceiling, it is chain-free, and Alfington is properly small and quiet, which suits the stated preference for somewhere more remote than a village centre. Against it: night storage heating and shared private drainage are both cost and hassle items that will show up on any survey, there is no sea within reach (Sidmouth is roughly 25 minutes), and it is about 20 minutes from each brother rather than the few miles the East Budleigh and Budleigh options manage.

parking.note: A carport measuring 4.18m x 2.58m, explicitly described in the listing as providing off-road parking — one vehicle, under cover, not a shared or permit arrangement.

properties.aiTake: Cheap, chain-free, quiet and — unusually for a village cottage at this price — it has its own carport, which is why it earns its place; it is held back by being properly inland with no coast and no brother nearby, plus night storage heating and shared private drainage to price in.

properties.title: Yonder Street, Ottery St Mary (2-bed cottage, downstairs bathroom)
properties.linkLabel: onthemarket.com — Yonder Street, Ottery St Mary
properties.body: A two-bedroom cottage on Yonder Street in the middle of Ottery St Mary, marketed with an established tenant already in place and therefore immediate rental income if that is wanted. The floorplan is the useful bit: 665 sq ft over two floors, with the living room (feature fireplace), dining room, kitchen AND the bathroom all on the ground floor, and the two double bedrooms upstairs. That downstairs bathroom is worth noting — very few cottages on this list have one. Outside there is a south-facing rear garden with a patio, a lawn and a substantial shed with a wood store, plus side access to the front. One legal detail flagged in the listing: rear pedestrian access carries a right of way in favour of the adjoining property. EPC D. Walking distance to Ottery's shops and amenities, with the A30, the M5 and the London Waterloo line all reachable. Only three photos are published, which is thin — it is a tenanted property, so interior access for photography was probably limited, and that also means limited insight into condition.
properties.why: The layout is the reason it is here. A ground-floor bathroom plus a ground-floor dining room means the long-term "no stairs" conversion is close to trivial — put a bed in the dining room and the whole thing works on one level, which is far better than the usual "adaptable in theory" cottage. At £210,000 it is comfortably in budget, it has a south-facing garden with a real shed, and it is a character cottage rather than a modern box. Against it: three photos is not enough to judge condition, it is a town-centre street rather than the remote setting Jesse leans towards, there is no coast (Sidmouth is about six miles), Ottery is roughly 20 minutes from both brothers, and the sitting tenant means viewing and vacant possession both need sorting out.

parking.note: The listing gives no parking detail — no driveway, garage or allocated space is claimed, and Yonder Street is a narrow through-street of terraced cottages fronting the pavement, so on-street is the realistic assumption. Researching it: East Devon District Council runs car parks in the centre of Ottery St Mary (the main one off Silver Street/Land of Canaan) within a few minutes' walk, and EDDC's virtual monthly permit scheme covers Ottery St Mary at £10/month for a single town with no permit to display. Devon County Council handles the on-street side; there is no residents' permit zone in Ottery, so unrestricted on-street stretches are first-come-first-served. One thing to check with the agent given the street: Devon County Council has had repeated temporary parking prohibitions and through-traffic closures on Yonder Street and neighbouring Mill Street during works (another closure is scheduled for late August 2026), which is a nuisance rather than a dealbreaker but does mean on-street parking here is occasionally suspended outright.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Ground-floor bathroom — rare on this list — and a substantial shed with wood store in a south-facing garden

properties.aiTake: The ground-floor bathroom and ground-floor dining room make this one of the easiest "no stairs later" conversions on the whole list, and at £210,000 with a south-facing garden it is fair value; it is dragged down by being inland and town-centre, ~20 minutes from either brother, with only three photos and a sitting tenant to work around.

properties.title: Hillside Court, The Marles, Exmouth (ground-floor flat)

flags.text: GROUND FLOOR (but steps down in communal area)
ON-STREET PARKING ONLY (garages to rent from freeholder)

properties.linkLabel: onthemarket.com — Hillside Court, The Marles, Exmouth
properties.body: A ground-floor flat in Hillside Court on The Marles, Exmouth, chain-free and newly to market. 742 sq ft: a 25'1" x 11'6" dual-aspect living/dining room, a high-specification kitchen with integrated Neff appliances, quartz worktops and a Quooker instant-boiling tap, two double bedrooms both with built-in wardrobes and LED lighting, and a fully tiled shower room with a walk-in shower. Engineered oak flooring, gas central heating, uPVC double glazing, plus a storage cupboard in the communal hallway. Council Tax B, EPC-relevant broadband at 67Mbps. Tenure is leasehold with roughly 92 years remaining, £250 a year ground rent and £120 a month covering service charge and buildings insurance. Parking is on-street on The Marles, which the agent calls ample; Hillside Court has garage blocks but they are rented from the freeholder on an as-and-when basis rather than sold with the flat, and some of those garages have a driveway too. One thing the listing is honest about and worth repeating: despite the ground-floor designation, there are steps down to the front door within the communal area. Note this is a different flat from the other Marles entry already on the list — that one is a Pennys listing at £200,000 with a garage included and a brand-new extended lease on completion, in the same EX8 4NE postcode.
properties.why: It is a cheap, chain-free, genuinely single-level Exmouth flat with a big living room and a kitchen someone has already spent real money on, at £189,950 — inside Jesse's actual target range rather than at the ceiling, and about as close to family as anything gets. The problems are the ones Bro 3 has already said he cares about: a 92-year lease is under the 100-plus he is comfortable with, £120 a month plus £250 a year ground rent is a standing cost, and the garage is rented from the freeholder rather than owned, so there is no parking that comes with the property. The steps down in the communal area also undercut the ground-floor advantage for the specific long-term scenario Jesse cares about. Included because it is a legitimate cheap Exmouth option worth having on the board, not because it is exciting.

parking.note: No parking is included in the sale. The listing states there is "ample on street parking" on The Marles, and that Hillside Court has several garage blocks which can be rented from the freeholder on an as-and-when basis — some with a driveway attached — but they are rented, not owned, and availability is not guaranteed at the point of purchase. Researching the location: The Marles is a residential estate road in the Withycombe area of Exmouth with no residents' permit scheme and no waiting restrictions, so on-street parking here is genuinely free and unrestricted rather than the permit-or-car-park situation the town-centre and village entries face — a practical positive. East Devon District Council's £10/month virtual town permit exists for Exmouth if a car park is ever needed, but for a flat on this estate it should not be. The thing to nail down with Links is whether a garage is actually available to rent now and at what rent, because it changes the effective monthly cost on top of the £120 service charge.

properties.aiTake: A cheap, chain-free, all-on-one-level Exmouth flat with a genuinely good kitchen and a 25ft living room at £189,950, close to family — but a 92-year lease, £120/month plus ground rent, no owned parking and communal steps down to the door keep it a practical option rather than a good one.

properties.title: Portland Avenue, Exmouth (ground-floor flat, garage + allocated space)

flags.text: SHARE OF FREEHOLD (997 yrs, £1,200/yr service charge)

properties.body: A ground-floor purpose-built flat in a small development of just four apartments, a short distance from Exmouth seafront, town centre, bus services and the health centre. Private front door off a communal hallway into a reception hall with fitted, linen and cylinder cupboards. A 16ft lounge/dining room to the front, and a kitchen/breakfast room with modern fitted units, integrated dishwasher, built-in oven and four-ring electric hob. Two double bedrooms and a bathroom/WC with both a bath and a separate shower cubicle with a Mira unit. Communal lawned gardens to the front; to the rear an allocated parking space and a single garage with an up-and-over door. Tenure is a quarter share of the freehold alongside a long lease with roughly 997 years remaining; service charge approximately £1,200 a year including buildings insurance.
properties.why: Of the cheap ground-floor flats that keep surfacing around Exmouth, this is the one that actually solves parking — an allocated space *and* a garage, in a block of only four, which is far better than the on-street compromise most of the others carry. Being ground-floor and level, it passes the long-term no-stairs test outright, and it has a proper bathroom with both bath and shower rather than a token shower room. Against that: it is an ordinary purpose-built flat with no character, the outside space is communal lawn rather than a garden of Jesse’s own, and the £1,200 annual service charge is a real recurring cost even though the 997-year lease and quarter share of the freehold make the tenure about as benign as leasehold gets.

parking.note: Both an allocated parking space and a single garage with an up-and-over door, at the rear of the development — stated explicitly in the listing, not inferred.

properties.aiTake: The rare cheap Exmouth ground-floor flat that comes with both a garage and an allocated space, in a block of only four and walkable to the seafront — but it is plain, the garden is communal, and there is a £1,200-a-year service charge against an otherwise benign 997-year lease with a share of freehold.

properties.title: Capel Lane, Exmouth (tucked-away bungalow)
properties.body: A well-presented semi-detached bungalow in a private, tucked-away position standing in generously sized mature front and rear gardens. Double-glazed entrance porch into a reception hall with a good-sized linen cupboard housing a modern Worcester boiler; bright 17ft lounge/dining room with sliding patio doors into a double-glazed conservatory overlooking the front gardens; kitchen with fitted units and space for appliances. Two double bedrooms, both with built-in wardrobes and looking over the rear gardens, and a modern shower room/WC. Gas central heating, double glazing throughout. A pedestrian gate from the rear garden gives access to the garage, which sits in a block close by. Offered with no ongoing chain.
properties.why: This is the practical end of the list rather than the characterful end, but it scores where it counts: a true bungalow, so the no-stairs long-term test is already passed with nothing to adapt, plus a garage, unusually generous mature gardens, and a genuinely private tucked-away setting rather than a village-centre frontage. Capel Lane sits on the north-eastern edge of Exmouth, which puts it closer to Woodbury Common’s trails and to Bro 2 than anything in the town centre while still being in Exmouth itself. What it does not have is character — this is a conventional post-war bungalow with a conservatory, not a cottage — and at £269,950 it costs noticeably more than the plainer Morton Road bungalow already tracked.

parking.note: A garage is included, sitting in a nearby block and reached through a pedestrian gate from the rear garden rather than from the property frontage. Worth knowing that this means no driveway at the bungalow itself, so anything larger than the garage, or a second car, falls back on the lane.

properties.aiTake: A chain-free bungalow with a garage, big mature gardens and a genuinely private tucked-away spot on the Woodbury-facing edge of Exmouth — already fully ground-floor for the long term, but conventional in character and dear at £269,950 next to the cheaper bungalows already on the list.

research.question: Routine sweep re-check: is this still listed, and has the price moved?
research.findings: Still live and confirmed on the market this sweep, but the asking price has come down from £269,950 to £250,000 — a £19,950 reduction. That moves it out of the £250k–£300k band and onto the £250,000 line exactly, which lifts its rating by a point under the budget weighting. Worth watching for a further drop given it has now been reduced once.

properties.title: Rolle Street, Exmouth (1991 store conversion, reverse-level)
properties.body: A two-bedroom freehold house converted by the current owners from a store room in 1991, tucked away behind Exmouth town centre. Reverse-level layout: the ground floor holds both bedrooms (each with a built-in wardrobe) and a brand-new fitted shower room with WC, while the first floor is a bright open-plan living area with a newly fitted contemporary kitchen. Recently renovated throughout — re-plastered and redecorated, new electrical fittings and lights, new floor coverings, new kitchen and shower room. Double glazing and modern electric heating. Within easy walking distance of the town centre, the train station and the seafront. Offered with no onward chain.
properties.why: Genuinely unusual in the way Jesse likes — a former store room someone turned into a house in 1991, tucked away behind the town rather than sitting in a row of identical terraces — and at £195,000 it is one of the few finds close to his real £170k target rather than the £300k ceiling. Freehold, no chain, freshly renovated so nothing needs immediate spending, and it is walkable to the seafront, the town and the train station in a way almost nothing else on this list manages at once. The trade-offs are real: no garden, no parking mentioned, and the reverse-level layout puts the kitchen and living space upstairs, which cuts against the long-term no-stairs test even though both bedrooms and the shower room are on the ground floor.

parking.note: The listing says nothing about parking either way, and the property sits in a tucked-away spot behind the town centre where a dedicated space would be unusual. Central Exmouth is covered by East Devon District Council pay-and-display car parks rather than a blanket residents’ permit zone, with the nearest large ones at Manor Gardens and the Magnolia Centre a few minutes’ walk away; some central streets carry time-limited restrictions. Because the exact frontage cannot be confirmed from the listing or photos, this is worth one direct question to Links before viewing — whether any on-street entitlement attaches to the property at all is the single unresolved point on an otherwise well-documented listing.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Converted from a store room in 1991 — a reverse-level house hidden behind the town centre, with bedrooms down and living up

properties.aiTake: A quirky freehold former store-room conversion, freshly renovated and chain-free at £195,000, within walking distance of the seafront, town and train station — no garden and no confirmed parking, and the reverse-level layout puts the living space upstairs.

properties.title: Town Lane, Woodbury (double-fronted period cottage)
properties.body: Double-fronted period cottage in central Woodbury with heavy exposed beams throughout. Cosy sitting room with a feature fireplace, a separate dining room, and a kitchen mixing rustic style with practical fittings. Three well-proportioned bedrooms upstairs alongside the bathroom. To the rear, a south-facing garden — private, sunny and a decent size — backed by a run of brick outbuildings under a corrugated roof giving real storage. Gas central heating, Council Tax Band A, EPC Rating E. what3words ///sitting.positives.grow
properties.why: Three bedrooms and genuine period character in Bro 2’s own village, with Woodbury Common and its trails a few minutes away and Darts Farm down the road. The south-facing rear garden is a proper one rather than a courtyard, and — worth noting given the scepticism about unphotographed outbuilding claims on the Newton Poppleford listing — the outbuildings here are clearly shown in the photos rather than just asserted in the copy. At £280,000 it is near the top of the range for a village-centre cottage with no parking of its own, which is exactly the "charming but pricey for what it is" shape that has drawn low marks before.

parking.note: The listing mentions no parking and none is visible in the photos — Town Lane is a narrow central village street, so it is on-street only. The practical backstop is the same one that applies to the other central-Woodbury entries: Flower Street car park (EX5 1LX) is free with a 23-hours-in-24 maximum stay and is a couple of minutes’ walk, and there is a further free car park beside Woodbury Village Hall. No residents’ permit scheme turned up for Woodbury, so this is unrestricted on-street plus two free car parks rather than a permit situation.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A run of brick outbuildings across the back of the south-facing garden — genuinely photographed, not just claimed in the copy

properties.aiTake: A beamy three-bed double-fronted cottage in Bro 2’s village with a sunny south-facing garden, real outbuildings and Woodbury Common on the doorstep — held back by no parking of its own, no train station nearby, and a £280,000 price that sits high for a village-centre cottage.

properties.title: High Street, East Budleigh (Grade II thatched cottage)

flags.text: NO PARKING (free village car park nearby)

properties.body: Thatched Grade II listed end-of-terrace cob cottage right in the heart of East Budleigh village. Ground floor: living room with exposed ceiling beams and a fireplace, opening to a second bedroom that also works as a home office or dining room, plus a bespoke modern kitchen with solid oak worktops, integral electric oven and induction hob, and a door out to the garden. First floor: one impressive double bedroom with a deep wardrobe, and a bathroom with a feature freestanding roll-top bath. Gas central heating, enclosed cottage-style rear garden with patio, shed and side gate. EPC exempt as a listed building; Council Tax Band B. Walking distance to the community shop, the church, the Sir Walter Raleigh pub and the free public car park.
properties.why: This is the closest thing to Jesse’s stated dream this list has had in a while and it is comfortably in budget: a genuinely thatched, genuinely listed cob cottage at £220,000, not a compromise version of one. It sits between both brothers — a couple of miles from Otterton, a short run to Woodbury — with East Budleigh Common and the Pebblebed Heaths trails effectively on the doorstep and Budleigh Salterton’s beach two miles down the road. The honest catch is parking: it fronts straight onto the road with no driveway, so it depends on the free village car park. There is a ground-floor room already usable as a bedroom, but the only bathroom is upstairs and listed-building consent would gate any change to that.

parking.note: No driveway, garage or allocated space — the cottage fronts directly onto the road, confirmed from the photos as well as the listing’s silence. The listing does point out it is "close to the free public car park", which matches what was already researched for the other East Budleigh entries: a small free 17-space car park just off the High Street (2-hour limit) plus the larger Hayes Lane car park a short walk away. There is no residents’ permit scheme in the village, so overnight parking means the car park or finding an unrestricted stretch of High Street — the same compromise every cottage on this street carries.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Thatched roof, exposed cob and ceiling beams, and a freestanding roll-top bath — EPC-exempt by virtue of being Grade II listed

properties.aiTake: A thatched Grade II cottage in the heart of East Budleigh with a ground-floor second bedroom and a proper cottage garden, now reduced to £200,000 — exactly the kind of character Jesse is after, and the only real drawback is that there is no parking.

research.question: Sweep re-check — is this still listed, and at what price?
research.findings: Still on the market and now cheaper. It has moved from the OnTheMarket listing at a £220,000 guide to a Hall & Scott listing on Rightmove at a £200,000 guide — a £20,000 reduction. The particulars are otherwise unchanged and confirm the same cottage: thatched Grade II listed end-of-terrace, living room with exposed ceiling beams and fireplace, bespoke modern kitchen with built-in oven and hob, ground-floor second bedroom/home office, impressive first-floor double bedroom, bathroom with a feature freestanding bath, gas central heating, cottage-style rear garden with shed, EPC exempt as a listed building, Council Tax Band B. At £200,000 this is now comfortably the cheapest thatched Grade II cottage on the tracked list, and it sits £30,000 above Jesse’s £170,000 target rather than £50,000 above it.

properties.title: Mount Pleasant Avenue, Exmouth (chain-free bungalow)
properties.body: A semi-detached two-double-bedroom bungalow in an elevated position in the Hulham part of Exmouth (EX8 4QW), on the north-eastern edge of town nearest the Woodbury Common side. Bright living room with a bay window and rooftop views, kitchen looking over the rear garden, two double bedrooms with picture windows, and a shower room. Freehold, chain-free. Driveway plus a detached garage, and a private, surprisingly spacious rear garden with level lawn, established hedging and mature trees. Honestly described as needing modernisation throughout, so there is real renovation potential to add value.
properties.why: Found on OnTheMarket. It is right at the top of the £300k budget and needs a full refresh, so it is not the cheap-and-cheerful end of the list, but as a package it lines up well with the stuff that actually matters long term: it is a proper single-storey bungalow (somewhere Jesse could stay put even if stairs became a problem one day), it is freehold, chain-free, and it comes with both a driveway and a detached garage plus a decent garden. The modernisation-needed angle is a plus rather than a minus if you want to put your own stamp on it and build in equity. Not much character in the building itself, and it is a town rather than remote-rural spot.
properties.aiTake: A practical, low-risk long-term home base — freehold, chain-free, single-storey, with driveway, garage and a good garden on the Woodbury Common edge of Exmouth — but it sits right at the £300k ceiling, needs full modernisation, and has little character of its own.

parking.note: Private driveway plus a detached garage, both included — comfortably ahead of the parking most Exmouth town properties offer, and the garage doubles as workshop/storage space.

properties.title: 21 George Street, Exmouth (tenanted investment)
properties.body: A semi-detached house on George Street, about 50 metres from Exmouth's high street and a 10-minute walk to the seafront, completely renovated three years ago. Open-plan living/dining area, a newly fitted galley kitchen with dishwasher, utility room, downstairs toilet, laminate flooring throughout the ground floor. Upstairs has two double bedrooms and one single, plus a bathroom with both bath and electric shower. Double glazing, private rear courtyard. Freehold. Currently occupied by tenants — marketed as a turnkey investment opportunity.
properties.why: Submitted directly by Jesse. Well inside budget, freehold, right in Exmouth town centre near the high street and a short walk to the seafront. The catch: it's currently tenanted and marketed as an investment property, so buying it for Jesse to actually live in would likely mean waiting out the tenancy or buying with vacant possession terms agreed separately — worth checking with the agent before getting attached. Parking isn't stated either way.
properties.aiTake: Solidly in-budget, freehold, and right in Exmouth town centre near the high street and a short walk to the seafront — but it's currently tenanted and marketed as an investment flip rather than a home ready to move into, and neither a garden nor parking is confirmed.

parking.note: Listed as "ask agent" — not confirmed either way. Exmouth introduced a residents' parking permit scheme in August 2023 covering parts of the town (including the Colonies area and parts of St Andrews Road) — George Street wasn't specifically named in what turned up, so it's worth checking directly with Devon County Council or the agent whether this address falls inside a permit zone before assuming casual on-street parking is available.

properties.title: The Beacon, Exmouth (Grade II garden apartment)
properties.body: A bright and spacious Grade II listed garden apartment in a period building on the historic Beacon, near the seafront and town centre. Open-plan living/kitchen area, a large double bedroom overlooking a patio, an occasional bedroom/study, a bathroom, and communal courtyard access. 1/5 share of freehold with the remainder of a 999-year lease, service charge approx £1,500/year. EPC E, Council Tax Band B. Chain-free.
properties.why: A third, distinct Beacon listing from the two already tracked — a different agent (Meadows), different price, and structured as a share-of-freehold rather than a standard lease. Grade II listed, chain-free, and in Jesse's favourite Exmouth pocket. Zoopla's Cloudflare block meant only one photo could be pulled this time rather than the full gallery — worth a second attempt next sweep.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Grade II listed period building on the historic Beacon, with a private patio and communal courtyard

properties.aiTake: A characterful, chain-free Grade II garden apartment in Jesse's favourite Exmouth pocket with a near-999-year lease (effectively freehold in practice) — the £1,500/year service charge and share-of-freehold structure are worth a clear eye, and only one photo could be recovered this sweep.

parking.note: Not mentioned in the listing. The Beacon sits right in Exmouth town centre near the seafront — on-street parking here is limited/restricted, and the nearest reliable option is one of the town-centre pay-and-display car parks a short walk away. Worth confirming directly with Meadows whether any allocated space comes with this specific unit before ruling it out.

properties.title: New Street, Exmouth (town-centre terrace)
properties.body: A characterful and beautifully presented 2 double bedroom terrace house in Exmouth town centre, a short walk from the train station and a level walk to the seafront. Entrance hallway, downstairs cloakroom, through sitting/dining room with a fireplace and French doors, and a modern kitchen with integrated appliances. Upstairs both double bedrooms have en-suite facilities. Enclosed rear courtyard garden with gated access, plus a brick utility store and timber shed. Gas central heating, double glazing. Freehold. Council Tax Band B.
properties.why: Jesse drove past this one and liked it. Genuinely characterful for a town-centre terrace (fireplace, French doors, both bedrooms en-suite), freehold, and close to the train station and seafront. The honest trade-off: no garage or dedicated parking at all, which would normally be a hard-requirement miss — flagged plainly rather than hidden.
properties.aiTake: A genuinely characterful freehold terrace right in Exmouth town centre, close to the train station and a level walk to the seafront — but it has no parking at all, which is a real miss against the hard requirement, and both bedrooms being upstairs with no ground-floor room rules out long-term stair-free living.

parking.note: No garage or dedicated parking with the property — confirmed directly in the listing. New Street is in Exmouth town centre; on-street parking here is metered/restricted rather than free, and the nearest pay-and-display options are the town-centre car parks a short walk away (e.g. around the Strand/seafront). Worth checking East Devon's residents' permit scheme for this specific postcode before assuming casual on-street parking is realistic.

properties.title: Morton Road, Exmouth (ground-floor bungalow)
properties.body: A freehold attached bungalow with a private courtyard/sun terrace and a dedicated parking space, close to Exmouth town centre and the seafront. Open-plan living room and kitchen with a built-in oven and hob, a double bedroom with wardrobe space, and a modern en-suite shower room. Electric heating and UPVC double glazing throughout. Council Tax Band A, EPC E. Pays a small (unstated) contribution towards the communal fire alarm system at 15 Morton Road. research.question: Look further into what you actually do for parking on The Strand, Lympstone.

Two car parks serve the immediate area: the free Lympstone Village Station car park right on The Strand (13 spaces, no permit needed, first-come-first-served, but can fill up with rail commuters), and Underhill Car Park a short walk away. Underhill's management has been unsettled for a while — East Devon District Council was in talks with Lympstone Parish Council years ago about the Parish taking it over and potentially issuing permits, and I couldn't confirm what, if anything, was finalised or whether a strict residents' scheme runs there now. Beyond that, East Devon District Council sells modular monthly/annual town permits for its pay-and-display car parks generally, but I couldn't confirm Lympstone is one of the towns those permits cover, nor find a price. Devon County Council handles on-street residents' permit zones separately and I couldn't confirm one exists for The Strand either. Bottom line: there's workable free/cheap parking nearby (the station car park is the best bet), but nothing deeded to the property and nothing guaranteed — worth a direct call to Lympstone Parish Council or East Devon's parking team before relying on it.

Leasehold: 99 years from July 2007 (~80 years remaining), ground rent £291/year, service charge £4,078/year with major works planned for 2026. Council tax band A, EPC D.
properties.why: Submitted by family — cheap headline price and genuinely ground floor, but two things need weighing before getting excited: an offer of £58,000 has already been received on it, with only 5 working days from the listing's publication for anyone to beat it, so this may already be gone or about to go; and the £4,078/year service charge (with major works flagged for 2026 on top) would eat a huge chunk of the low purchase price over time. Family's own note flagged "no place to park, worrisome back roof" — parking isn't mentioned in the listing but Victoria Road has a residents' Zone B permit scheme for on-street parking; roof condition isn't addressed in the listing text either and would need a direct question to the agent or a viewing.
properties.aiTake: Cheapest thing on the whole list and genuinely ground-floor near the seafront, but a £58,000 offer already on the table and a punishing £4,078/year service charge (with major works pending) undercut the headline price badly — worth a very quick decision if pursued at all, not a leisurely one.

parking.note: Not mentioned in the listing. Victoria Road has Limited Waiting restrictions (Mon-Sat 8am-6pm, 1hr no return) with an exemption for Residents' Zone B permit holders — a resident's permit (around £35/year for a first permit) would be needed for reliable on-street parking rather than free unrestricted parking.

properties.title: Chapel Street, Sidbury (ground-floor flat)
properties.body: Purpose-built one-bedroom ground-floor flat in a small development in Sidbury village. Dual-aspect sitting/dining room overlooking communal gardens, modern kitchen with Corian worktops and built-in oven, double bedroom with built-in wardrobe, bathroom with electric shower. Communal gardens extend down to the River Sid with a walking path. Village shop, pub, primary school and bus links nearby. Leasehold, term expiring 24.03.2113 (~87 years remaining). Reduced 06/06/2026.
properties.why: The cheapest thing on the whole list at £140,000, and explicitly ground floor, but it's a real outlier geographically — Sidbury is inland near Sidmouth, further from both Woodbury Common and both brothers than anywhere else being tracked. Worth keeping on file purely as a rock-bottom-price, no-stairs option, but it's a fallback shape, not a first choice.
properties.aiTake: Rock-bottom price and genuinely ground-floor, which counts for a lot, but Sidbury is well off the beaten path relative to both the coast and the brothers, and there's no character or parking to speak of — a fallback option rather than a contender.

parking.note: Listing doesn't specify parking arrangements for this flat — worth asking the agent directly, since purpose-built developments like this sometimes have allocated bays not mentioned in the online listing.

properties.title: Bicton Street, Exmouth (Grade II townhouse + separate listed barn)

flags.text: HAS PARKING (off-road + rear space by barn)

properties.body: Substantial six-bedroom Grade II listed period townhouse over three floors in Exmouth, needing renovation, no onward chain. Two reception rooms, spacious kitchen/breakfast room, ground-floor bedroom with en-suite wet room, plus five further bedrooms across the upper floors. Wall-enclosed rear garden, gas central heating, solar water heating tubes. The standout feature: a separate Grade II listed brick barn (18' x 10') in the walled garden, suitable for a studio, workshop, or storage subject to consent. Off-road parking plus a rear space by the barn. Close to town centre, beach, and the railway station.
properties.why: Significantly over budget and needs real renovation work, but it's genuinely one of a kind — a Grade II townhouse with its own separate listed barn, right in Exmouth with off-road parking and no chain. The barn alone is the kind of oddball workshop/studio space Jesse likes flagged. Included as an exceptional/unique find despite the price, per the standing rule for unusual properties — but six bedrooms and renovation work make this a much bigger project than most of what's on the list.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A separate Grade II listed brick barn (18'x10') in the walled rear garden — usable as a studio, workshop, or storage subject to consent. A genuinely rare feature this close to Exmouth town centre.

properties.aiTake: A one-of-a-kind find — Grade II townhouse plus its own listed barn, in Exmouth with real off-road parking — but it's £115,000 over budget, needs renovation throughout, and six bedrooms is far more house than needed, so the price adjustment weighs it down despite the character.

parking.note: Off-road parking plus a rear parking space adjacent to the barn, confirmed in the listing.

properties.title: 1 Castle Cottages, Castle Lane, Woodbury (period cottage)
properties.body: Recently upgraded period cottage in a central Woodbury village location, no onward chain. Modern kitchen/dining room with utility, spacious sitting room, an office/4th-bedroom option, three double bedrooms (ensuite master), main bathroom. Private courtyard garden with a useful storage shed. Parking to the front. Electric boiler heating. Note: a neighbouring property has a Right of Way to access a drain located in the garden.
properties.why: A different Castle Lane cottage to the thatched one already on file, this one in Woodbury itself rather than Exmouth — genuinely close to a brother and the Common's trails, with real parking to the front (still not common on this list) and a storage shed. £75,000 over budget and not Grade II listed, but it's beautifully presented, no-chain, and move-in ready rather than needing work.
properties.aiTake: A genuinely nice, move-in-ready Woodbury cottage with real front parking and a storage shed, close to a brother and the Common — but £75,000 over budget and not particularly unusual architecturally, so it lands as a solid rather than standout option.

parking.note: "Parking to the front" listed as a key feature.

properties.title: Vicarage Road, East Budleigh (stone and cob period cottage)
properties.body: Stone and cob period cottage in East Budleigh with deceptively large accommodation. Ground floor: large living room, spacious kitchen/dining room, cloakroom, utility area. Upstairs: two bedrooms and a bathroom. South-facing, very secluded garden with well-fenced boundaries and a summerhouse (a neighbour has a right-of-way for access). Sits within the East Devon AONB, around 2 miles from the sea and 10 miles from Exeter. Freehold, parking included. Reduced 20/08/2025.
properties.why: A characterful stone-and-cob cottage with real parking and a genuinely private, secluded garden complete with a summerhouse — only £25,000 over budget, which is a modest stretch for what's on offer. East Budleigh keeps it close to the Otterton brother, and the AONB setting fits the rural-over-village-centre preference well.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A secluded south-facing garden with its own summerhouse

properties.aiTake: Genuine character, real parking, and an unusually private secluded garden with a summerhouse, close to the Otterton brother — only a modest £25,000 over budget, which makes this one of the more reasonable over-budget stretches on the list.

parking.note: Parking confirmed in the listing details, though exact arrangement (driveway vs allocated space) isn't spelled out.

properties.title: Cranes Lane, East Budleigh (renovated period cottage)
properties.body: Fully renovated terraced period cottage in East Budleigh. Entrance hall, sitting room, kitchen/dining room, cloakroom/WC, bathroom, two double bedrooms. Modern gas central heating and double glazing throughout. Attractive, low-maintenance courtyard garden with a wildlife pond and seating area. No allocated parking, but a public car park is around 130 yards away. Freehold. Added 21/02/2026.
properties.why: Unlike most of the character cottages on this list, this one is already fully renovated — modern heating, double glazing, nothing left to do. A wildlife pond in the courtyard garden is a nice unusual touch. The real drawback is parking: nothing allocated, just a public car park roughly 130 yards off, and it's £25,000 over budget.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A courtyard garden with its own wildlife pond

properties.aiTake: The one cottage on the list that's already fully renovated — nothing to do on move-in, plus a nice wildlife pond in the courtyard — but no allocated parking and £25,000 over budget pull it down despite the move-in-ready appeal.

parking.note: No allocated parking with the property. A public car park is roughly 130 yards away — realistically walkable but not guaranteed, and worth checking East Budleigh's car park capacity/cost before relying on it day-to-day.

properties.title: Greenway, Woodbury (Grade II listed cottage)
properties.body: Grade II listed period cottage in the heart of Woodbury village, arranged over three floors: sitting room with fireplace and alcove storage, kitchen/dining room, two bedrooms, plus a loft room with a vaulted ceiling and exposed beams (fitted with its own shower, usable as an occasional third bedroom or reception room). Front patio with lawn and a vegetable patch, a brick-built storage shed. On-street parking. Freehold, EPC C, council tax band B. Reduced on 13/05/2026.
properties.why: A second, distinct Greenway property from the one already tracked — this one is Grade II listed, spread over three floors with a genuinely useful loft room (vaulted ceiling, exposed beams, its own shower), and £30k under the hard budget ceiling. Right in Woodbury village centre, so a short walk from a brother and effectively on the doorstep of Woodbury Common. Same trade-off as most Woodbury-centre finds: on-street parking only, though the village has a free short-stay car park (Flower Street) a couple of minutes away if visitors need it.

checklist.uniqueFeature: A loft room with a vaulted ceiling, exposed beams and its own shower — usable as an occasional third bedroom

properties.aiTake: Grade II character, a genuinely useful loft room, freehold, and comfortably under budget right in Woodbury village — let down only by on-street-only parking, which is the standard trade-off for anything this central.

parking.note: On-street parking only, confirmed directly in the listing — no allocated space or garage. Woodbury village centre has a free short-stay car park on Flower Street a couple of minutes' walk away, as already established for other village-centre Woodbury entries.

properties.title: Clarence Road, Budleigh Salterton (end-of-terrace)

parking.note: Off-road parking directly in front for two cars.

properties.body: Spacious three-bedroom end-of-terrace close to Budleigh Salterton town centre and seafront, with two stone fireplaces (gas fires) in the open-plan living/dining room, oak flooring in the reception hall, built-in bedroom storage and window shutters. Enclosed rear brick-paviour courtyard garden with a pedestrian gate onto Greenway Lane. Freehold, level access at the front.
properties.why: Genuine off-road parking for two cars, freehold, and three bedrooms in a coastal town — a plain but solid option, right at the top of budget.
properties.aiTake: A solid, no-drama parking-and-freehold pick in a coastal town, but the character here is two fireplaces rather than the building itself, and it sits right at your budget ceiling.

properties.title: Flat 3 Ashley House, Raddenstile Lane, Exmouth (ground-floor flat) — AUCTION

parking.note: One allocated parking space included with the flat.

properties.body: Vacant ground-floor flat close to Exmouth town centre, seafront and the Exeter branch line — lounge/diner with kitchen access, master bedroom with en-suite shower room, second bedroom, family bathroom, private courtyard and use of communal gardens. Secure intercom entry, gas central heating, double glazing.
properties.why: Cheap, explicitly ground-floor, comes with an allocated parking space and is effectively freehold (967-year share of freehold) — ticks the flat exception cleanly. It's going to auction on 10 September 2026 with only a guide price, so the eventual sale price could move up.
properties.aiTake: A cheap, practical box-ticker — ground floor, parking, effectively freehold, close to Exmouth centre, train and sea — but it's a plain block flat going to auction, so treat £155k as a floor, not a likely final price.

properties.title: The Strand, Lympstone (2-bed semi-detached cottage)

parking.note: Listing says 'Ask agent' rather than confirming anything. The Strand itself has no dedicated resident bays — parking there is on-street with no confirmed residents' permit zone. The free Lympstone Village Station car park right on The Strand (13 spaces, no permit needed, first-come-first-served, but can fill with rail commuters) and Underhill Car Park a short walk away are the two nearby options; Underhill's permit/management status has been unsettled historically. Nothing is deeded to this property — worth a direct call to the agent or Lympstone Parish Council before relying on it.

properties.body: Two-bedroom semi-detached cottage in the heart of Lympstone village — open-plan living space with fitted kitchen, dining room and a sitting room with exposed ceiling beams, both bedrooms and a shower room upstairs, gas central heating, patio sun terrace shared with two neighbouring cottages. Freehold, no onward chain, new boiler due to be fitted March 2026.
properties.why: A genuine cottage in Lympstone village with no chain and exposed beams, but parking isn't confirmed and it's priced right at the budget ceiling — a stretch case worth flagging rather than a clean fit.
properties.aiTake: Village-centre cottage charm and no chain, but unconfirmed parking and a price right at the ceiling make this a stretch rather than a clean fit — worth checking with the agent before ruling in or out.

properties.title: Cranford Avenue, Exmouth (ground-floor flat, garage)

parking.note: Garage with up-and-over door included with the property.

properties.body: Well-proportioned ground-floor apartment in the Avenues area of Exmouth, overlooking communal gardens with mature trees and shrubs. Sitting/dining room with patio access, modern kitchen/breakfast room, two double bedrooms, wet room with electric shower, 710 sq ft. Includes a garage with up-and-over door. No onward chain. Leasehold, approx. 78 years remaining, service charge ~£1,828/yr, ground rent £152/yr.
properties.why: Ground-floor, a real garage (not just a space), and no chain — a genuinely distinct unit from the other Cranford Avenue flat already tracked, though the ~78-year lease and service charges are worth weighing.
properties.aiTake: Ground floor with an actual garage and no chain is a rare combo for a flat, but a 78-year lease plus ~£1,828/yr service charge chips into the value — a fair option, not a standout.

properties.title: The Old Court House, Woodbury
properties.body: A two-bedroom first-floor apartment within a converted 1834 Grade II listed building in the centre of Woodbury, converted to residential use in 2012. It has high ceilings, period sash windows, a dual-aspect kitchen/living room with fireplace, and countryside views. Recent upgrades include new windows in 2024 (around £20,000) and electric heating installed in 2023. Two private storage sheds are included, and the sale is a 25% share of the freehold with a 185-year lease remaining. Council tax band A, offered with no onward chain.
properties.why: At offers over £150,000 this is the cheapest of this sweep's finds by a wide margin, and it sits in Woodbury itself, close to Woodbury Common and one of your brothers. The character is genuine (Grade II, 1834, sash windows, fireplace) rather than cosmetic. Set against that: it's a first-floor flat with no garden, a lease rather than outright freehold (albeit with a 25% freehold share and 185 years left), and parking isn't mentioned anywhere in the listing, so don't assume a space comes with it.

checklist.uniqueFeature: 25% share of freehold in a converted 1834 Grade II listed courthouse building, with two private storage sheds

properties.aiTake: Cheapest of the batch with real period character and a Woodbury Common location, but it's a leasehold first-floor flat with no garden and no disclosed parking.

parking.note: Not stated anywhere in the listing. Woodbury has no formal residents' permit scheme, so on-street parking on the surrounding village lanes is the realistic default for a central converted building like this — worth confirming directly with the agent (Butt Estates, Topsham) before assuming a space is included.

properties.title: Bell Street, Otterton
properties.body: A two-bedroom terraced cottage on Bell Street in Otterton, suitable as a permanent or holiday home, with the roof fully renewed in 2023. The ground floor has an entrance hall, sitting room with fireplace, kitchen/breakfast room, rear lobby and shower room; the first floor has two bedrooms and a bathroom. There's an attractive enclosed rear garden with raised beds, an artificial lawn, a woodchip area and a timber store. Freehold, council tax band C, mains electric, water and drainage, offered with no onward chain.
properties.why: £220,000 for a freehold cottage with its own garden in Otterton, a short distance from your brother nearby, is a solid budget fit. It has genuine cottage character (fireplace, terraced village form) without being a fixer-upper — the roof was redone in 2023. The honest catch is parking: the listing states on-street parking subject to availability, and Otterton has no public car park of its own, so on-street is genuinely the only option here, not a gap in the listing. Distinct from the already-tracked "3 Bell Street" (a different Rightmove/Pennys listing, same street).

checklist.uniqueFeature: Roof fully renewed in 2023; enclosed rear garden with raised beds, artificial lawn and timber store

properties.aiTake: Solidly in-budget freehold cottage with a real garden and a brother nearby, let down only by Otterton's genuine lack of any parking beyond the street.

parking.note: Listing confirms on-street parking, subject to availability. Otterton has no public car park in the village and no confirmed residents' permit scheme, so on-street really is the norm here rather than a detail the agent omitted.

properties.title: Greenway, Woodbury (cob-and-stone cottage)
properties.body: A two-bedroom character cottage occupying a pedestrianised position in the heart of Woodbury village, with good access to local amenities. It has exposed ceiling beams and an inglenook-style fireplace with a wood-burning stove, a first-floor modern bathroom, a lounge/dining room, a modern kitchen and gas central heating. There are front and rear gardens. Offered with no onward chain, in a popular village location with good access to Exmouth, Exeter and the main link roads.
properties.why: Right in the middle of your budget at £265,000, with the best character features of this sweep's finds — exposed beams, inglenook fireplace, wood burner — plus its own front and rear gardens, which is rare for a cottage this central. It's in Woodbury itself, so close to your brother and Woodbury Common. The tradeoff is the pedestrianised village-centre position: the listing gives no parking detail at all, and a cottage with no direct vehicle access to its door means on-street parking elsewhere in the village is the likely reality, not a guaranteed space. Note: distinct from the already-tracked "greenwaygradeii" and "greenwaywoodbury" entries — Greenway appears to be a common street/place name in Woodbury with several separate cottages on file.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Cob-and-stone cottage with inglenook fireplace and wood-burning stove, in a pedestrianised part of Woodbury village centre, with both front and rear gardens

properties.aiTake: The most characterful cottage of this sweep's batch with a genuine garden and a Woodbury Common location, but its pedestrianised village-centre position means parking is a real unknown, not just an unstated detail.

parking.note: Not stated in the listing, and the cottage sits in a pedestrianised part of the village with no obvious direct vehicle access to the door. Woodbury has no formal residents' permit scheme, so any parking would be on-street on a nearby lane — worth checking with the agent before relying on it.

properties.title: St. Johns Farm Mews, Exmouth
properties.body: A two-bedroom house in St. Johns Farm Mews, a small mews-style development off St Johns Road in a semi-rural setting on the northern edge of Exmouth. It has two double bedrooms with fitted wardrobes, a spacious lounge/dining room, a modern updated kitchen, and a recently renovated shower room with a rainfall feature; the master bedroom has a vanity area. There's a front garden, a garage, and additional off-street and communal parking. The listing describes the finish as beautifully decorated throughout with contemporary touches and notes excellent transport links.
properties.why: The standout here is parking: a garage plus off-street and communal spaces, which the agent rightly calls a rare find in this kind of location, and it's the only one of this sweep's finds with a real answer to your parking requirement. It's in Exmouth, so close to the coast and reasonably close to family, though the Mews sits north of the town centre in a quieter semi-rural pocket rather than right on the seafront. The tradeoff is character: this reads as a modern, tidily renovated house rather than a period property, so it's the practical pick rather than the charming one, and at offers over £295,000 it could end up pushing toward your ceiling.

checklist.uniqueFeature: Includes its own garage plus off-street and communal parking, unusually generous for the area

properties.aiTake: The parking answer of the group (garage plus off-street), in Exmouth, but modern and character-free, and "offers over £295,000" leaves room for the price to drift toward the ceiling.

parking.note: Listing states a garage plus off-street and communal parking are included — the clearest parking answer of this sweep's finds, though "communal" suggests some spaces may be shared rather than exclusively allocated, worth confirming with the agent (Hunters, Exeter).

properties.title: Woodbury (Grade II Listed one-bed cottage)
properties.body: A one-bedroom Grade II Listed cottage in Woodbury village, with exposed ceiling beams and a feature fireplace in the sitting room, a separate study, recently-fitted kitchen, and a ground-floor bathroom. Upstairs is a single double bedroom with a walk-in wardrobe. Enclosed rear garden with patio and decking. Freehold. Marketed by East of Exe, Topsham.
properties.why: Cheap, genuinely characterful, freehold, and right in Woodbury near Bro 2 and Woodbury Common's trails — the trade-off is that it's a small one-bed with no off-street parking, so it suits a single-person or downsizer scenario more than a family home.
properties.aiTake: A cheap, genuinely characterful Grade II cottage right in Woodbury near Bro 2 — but it's a tiny one-bed with no off-street parking, so it trades space and convenience for charm and price.

parking.note: On-street parking only, but Woodbury village has a small free short-stay car park (Flower Street) within a couple of minutes' walk, same as noted for the Mirey Lane cottage already tracked — a realistic fallback if the street itself is full.

properties.title: Cliff Road, Budleigh Salterton (ground-floor flat, sea views)
properties.body: A genuinely ground-floor, two-double-bedroom apartment in a small modern block (12 units) on Cliff Road, Budleigh Salterton, with a south-facing terrace looking over the communal garden towards the sea. Open-plan sitting room with sea views and patio access, fitted kitchen with appliances, separate WC plus a modern bathroom. One allocated parking space, with additional visitor parking. Direct access to the coastal footpath via the communal gardens. Share of freehold, 999-year lease from 1982 (roughly 955 years remaining), service charge £200/month. Chain-free. EPC C, very low flood risk.
properties.why: Clears the flats bar cleanly — genuinely ground-floor, cheap, chain-free, and with real allocated parking, which is unusual for a sub-£250k flat here. The sea view and direct coastal footpath access from a shared garden are a real plus for a flat at this price. It's a modern block rather than anything characterful, and the communal garden isn't private, but the near-999-year lease means it behaves like freehold in practice. A solid, low-drama fallback rather than a dream find.

checklist.uniqueFeature: South-facing terrace with a sea view plus direct access to the coastal footpath via the communal gardens

properties.aiTake: A genuinely ground-floor, sea-view flat with real allocated parking and a near-freehold-length lease — practical and cheap, if short on character.

parking.note: One allocated parking space included, plus additional visitor parking on site — confirmed in the listing.
